name: Rapamycin
description: Rapamycin is a macrolide compound that functions as a molecular glue by simultaneously binding FKBP12 and the FRB domain of mTOR (FRAP), forming a ternary complex. This interaction inhibits mTORC1 signaling, leading to immunosuppressive and antiproliferative effects. Structural studies reveal rapamycin's critical role in stabilizing the FKBP12-FRB interface, disrupting mTOR's kinase activity. Key findings highlight its utility as a chemical probe for mTOR pathway modulation and as a template for developing FKBP12-dependent molecular glues.

name: C49-Methyl rapamycin
description: C49-Methyl rapamycin is a rapamycin derivative where the C49 position is methylated. Like rapamycin, it functions as a molecular glue by simultaneously binding FKBP12 and the FRB domain of FRAP, forming a ternary complex. This interaction inhibits FRAP's kinase activity, disrupting mTOR signaling pathways. The methyl modification at C49 may alter binding kinetics or stability but retains the core mechanism of inducing FKBP12-FRB proximity.

name: Brefeldin A
description: Brefeldin A is a macrocyclic lactone fungal metabolite that acts as a potent inhibitor of Arf activation by selectively targeting the Sec7 domain of large ArfGEFs (BIG/GBF subfamilies). It stabilizes abortive Arf-GEF complexes, blocking GDP/GTP exchange and disrupting Golgi trafficking. Its molecular glue properties derive from simultaneous binding to Arf-GDP and the Sec7 domain, inducing a non-productive ternary complex. Key studies show it inhibits GBF1 and BIG1/2 with IC50 values in the low micromolar range, making it a critical tool for studying Arf-dependent vesicular transport.

name: (R,R)-2a
description: (S,S)-2a is the enantiomer of (R,R)-2a, sharing identical dimeric arylpropylsulfonamide architecture but with inverted stereochemistry. While docking predicted symmetrical binding akin to (R,R)-2a, pharmacological evaluation revealed lower potency, emphasizing the stereospecific nature of interactions with the CTZ-binding sites. This underscores the importance of chiral matching for optimal receptor modulation.

name: C15-(R)-Methylthienyl rapamycin
description: C15-(R)-Methylthienyl rapamycin features a thienyl group with (R)-methyl substitution at C15. It maintains rapamycin's molecular glue properties, bridging FKBP12 and FRB to inhibit mTOR signaling. The (R)-methylthienyl moiety may enhance hydrophobic interactions or modulate conformational flexibility, potentially influencing ternary complex formation efficiency. Structural studies suggest such modifications preserve the critical FKBP12- and FRB-binding interfaces while fine-tuning pharmacological properties.

name: Abscisic Acid
description: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a phytohormone that regulates plant growth, stress responses, and developmental processes such as seed dormancy and stomatal closure. It binds to PYL3/RCAR13 receptors, promoting the formation of monomeric PYL3 and enhancing PP2C inhibition efficiency. Structural studies reveal ABA-bound PYL3 forms trans-homodimers, distinct from other PYL family members, suggesting a unique regulatory mechanism. ABA's preferential localization in seed chalazal regions correlates with PYL3's high expression during seed development.

name: Ifenprodil
description: Ifenprodil is a phenylethanolamine compound that allosterically inhibits GluN1/GluN2B NMDA receptors by binding at the heterodimer interface of their amino-terminal domains (ATDs). It exhibits neuroprotective activity with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 320 nM. Structural studies reveal that ifenprodil stabilizes the GluN1b-GluN2B ATD heterodimer, restricting conformational freedom in the GluN2B ATD essential for channel inhibition. Its binding site involves residues from both GluN1b R1 and GluN2B R1/R2 domains, distinct from zinc-binding sites.

name: FK506
description: FK506 (tacrolimus) is a macrolide immunosuppressant that forms a binary complex with FKBP12, which then binds calcineurin to inhibit its phosphatase activity. The FKBP12-FK506 complex sterically blocks substrate access to calcineurin's active site without direct interaction with the catalytic center. This inhibition disrupts T-cell activation by preventing NF-AT dephosphorylation, thereby suppressing IL-2 production. The X-ray structure reveals FK506's role as a molecular glue, bridging FKBP12 and calcineurin via a composite interface distinct from the phosphatase active site.

name: Tafamidis
description: Tafamidis is a selective transthyretin (TTR) kinetic stabilizer that binds with negative cooperativity to the two thyroxine-binding sites of the TTR tetramer (Kds ∼2 nM and ∼200 nM). It inhibits amyloidogenesis by stabilizing the weaker dimer-dimer interface, preventing tetramer dissociation—the rate-limiting step in TTR fibril formation. Demonstrated efficacy in Phase II/III trials for TTR-FAP, tafamidis dose-dependently stabilizes both wild-type and mutant TTR (V30M, V122I) with EC50 values of 2.7–3.2 μM. Crystal structures confirm its binding mode and kinetic stabilization mechanism.

name: RO-2443
description: RO-2443 is an indolyl hydantoin compound that acts as a dual MDM2/MDMX antagonist by inducing protein dimerization. It binds the p53-binding pockets of both proteins with similar potency (MDM2 IC50 = 33 nM, MDMX IC50 = 41 nM). Structural studies show it occupies two subpockets (Phe and Trp) while inducing MDMX dimer formation (24.1 kDa complex). The binding is entropy-driven (Kd = 78 nM by ITC) and effectively stabilizes p53, activating apoptosis in MDMX-overexpressing cancer cells.

name: Trifluoperazine
description: Trifluoperazine (TFP) is a phenothiazine derivative that binds the hydrophobic cleft of Ca²⁺-S100A4, inducing pentameric oligomerization. Structural studies reveal two TFP molecules bind per S100A4 subunit without major protein conformational changes. TFP-mediated oligomerization disrupts S100A4's interaction with myosin-IIA, inhibiting its depolymerization activity. NMR and crystallography confirm binding occurs in solution. Inhibition correlates with oligomer formation, demonstrating a molecular glue mechanism where TFP bridges S100A4 dimers into higher-order assemblies.

name: Inositol tetraphosphate
description: Inositol tetraphosphate (Ins(1,4,5,6)P₄) acts as an essential intermolecular glue in the HDAC3-SMRT-DAD complex, bridging the interface between the proteins. It binds in a highly basic pocket, forming hydrogen bonds and salt bridges with both HDAC3 and SMRT-DAD. Its presence neutralizes charge repulsion, enabling complex assembly and HDAC3 activation. The specificity for Ins(1,4,5,6)P₄ suggests a regulatory role in HDAC3 recruitment, with implications for transcriptional control and potential therapeutic targeting.

name: Phenylurea
description: Phenylurea (PHU) is a weak modulator of small-conductance Ca2+-activated potassium (SK) channels, binding at the calmodulin (CaM)-channel interface of the CaM N-lobe. X-ray crystallography reveals its interaction with residues from both CaM and the channel's CaM-binding domain (CaMBD). PHU's urea group exhibits flip-flop conformational flexibility within the binding pocket. Structurally, it resembles more potent SK/IK channel modulators like 1-EBIO, suggesting it represents a primitive scaffold for this compound class.

name: 1-EBIO
description: 1-Ethyl-2-benzimidazolinone (1-EBIO) is a prototype small-molecule potentiator of SK/IK channels, though it suffers from low potency (sub-millimolar EC50) and limited selectivity. It shares structural similarities with phenylurea, binding at the CaM-channel interface. 1-EBIO reduces neuronal excitability and demonstrates neuroprotective effects in seizure and cerebral ischemia models. Its mechanism involves enhancing channel activity via CaM-dependent pathways, but its clinical utility is hindered by poor pharmacokinetic properties.

name: NS309
description: NS309 is a potent small-molecule modulator of SK/IK channels, acting as a molecular glue to stabilize the intrinsically disordered fragment (IDF) connecting S6 and the CaM-binding domain. It induces a structured conformation in the IDF, enhancing channel open probability at fixed Ca²⁺ concentrations. NS309's binding to the CaM–CaMBD complex facilitates coupling between Ca²⁺ sensing and mechanical channel gating, making it a key tool for studying SK channel activation and a template for drug development targeting disordered protein regions. [Empty line]

name: Brassinolide
description: Brassinolide is a plant steroid hormone that binds to the leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain of the receptor kinase BRI1, initiating brassinosteroid signaling. It induces conformational changes in BRI1, including ordering of the island domain, which facilitates heteromerization with somatic embryogenesis receptor kinases (SERKs). This ligand-dependent interaction activates downstream signaling through transphosphorylation of kinase domains. Brassinolide's binding is critical for plant growth and development, and its mechanism underpins the targeting of BRI1 antagonists.

name: CC-0651
description: CC-0651 is a small-molecule inhibitor of the E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme Cdc34A. It binds to a cryptic pocket on Cdc34A, distinct from the active site, and stabilizes the weak interaction between ubiquitin and the donor ubiquitin-binding site. Structural studies reveal CC-0651 forms a composite binding pocket with Cdc34A and ubiquitin, impeding catalysis without disrupting E2-E3 RING domain interactions. This molecular glue mechanism inhibits ubiquitin transfer and stabilizes the Cdc34A-ubiquitin thioester, demonstrating targeted disruption of UPS enzyme dynamics.

name: BRD4(1) compound 2
description: Compound 2 is a bivalent BET inhibitor featuring a chlorotriazole motif in its triazolopyridazine (TPDZ) core, which mimics the methyltriazole of i-BET762. It induces BRD4(1) dimerization via simultaneous engagement of two acetyl-lysine binding sites, with pKd values of 7.2 (BRD4(1)) and 6.1 (BRD4(2)). Cellular assays show potent c-Myc downregulation and growth inhibition in BRD4-sensitive cell lines (pGI50 7.3 in MM.1S). X-ray crystallography confirms its unique in cis bivalent binding mode.

name: BRD4(1) compound 6
description: Compound 6 (biBET) is a pseudosymmetrical bivalent probe with dual TPDZ motifs, replacing the piperazinone of earlier analogs. It exhibits exceptional potency (pKd 11 for tandem BRD4 domains) and slow dissociation kinetics. Cellular EC50 for BRD4-mediator complex disruption is 100 pM, making it the most potent BET probe reported. Its design validates simultaneous dual-domain targeting for enhanced pharmacological effects.

name: S-Lenalidomide
description: S-Lenalidomide is an immunomodulatory drug (IMiD) that binds CRBN, the substrate receptor of the CRL4CRBN E3 ubiquitin ligase. It induces degradation of CK1α by recruiting it to the ligase complex via a β-hairpin loop interaction. The compound's phthalimide ring forms critical contacts with CK1α and CRBN, enabling selective degradation. S-Lenalidomide exhibits higher affinity for CK1α than thalidomide or pomalidomide, explaining its clinical efficacy in del(5q) MDS. Its stereochemistry influences target specificity and binding efficiency.

name: CC-885
description: CC-885 is a cereblon modulator that induces CRL4CRBN-dependent ubiquitination and degradation of GSPT1, a translation termination factor. It exhibits potent anti-tumor activity, particularly in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cells, with sub-nanomolar potency. Structural studies reveal that CC-885 binds cereblon and recruits GSPT1 via a surface turn containing a critical glycine residue. Unlike lenalidomide or pomalidomide, CC-885 uniquely targets GSPT1 without degrading Ikaros or CK1α, demonstrating its distinct substrate specificity. Its mechanism involves a common structural degron shared with other cereblon substrates.

name: BMS-8
description: BMS-8 is a (2-methyl-3-biphenylyl)methanol-based small molecule that binds directly to PD-L1, as confirmed by NMR chemical shift perturbations. It stabilizes PD-L1 dimers, occluding the PD-1 interaction surface. With an IC50 in the nanomolar range, it effectively disrupts PD-1/PD-L1 complex formation. Structural studies reveal its binding induces conformational changes in PD-L1, blocking immune checkpoint signaling.

name: BMS-202
description: BMS-202 is a potent PD-L1 inhibitor from the (2-methyl-3-biphenylyl)methanol class, exhibiting sub-100 nM IC50 in disrupting PD-1/PD-L1 interactions. NMR data confirm direct binding to PD-L1, inducing dimerization and sterically hindering PD-1 engagement. Its mechanism involves occupying key hydrophobic pockets on PD-L1, validated by crystallographic studies.

name: JHRE06
description: JHRE06 is a 1,4-dihydroquinolin-4-one derivative functioning as a ​​molecular glue​​ that targets the REV1 C-terminal domain (CTD). It selectively binds a shallow, evolutionarily conserved surface on REV1 CTD (IC50= 0.78 μM), inducing ​​asymmetric dimerization​​ of REV1. This dimerization sterically occludes the REV7-binding interface, disrupting the REV1-REV7 protein-protein interaction (PPI) critical for mutagenic translesion synthesis (TLS) polymerase ζ recruitment. JHRE06 enhances cisplatin cytotoxicity in cancer cells (e.g., A375 melanoma, HT1080 fibrosarcoma) by ​​suppressing error-prone TLS​​, reducing mutation frequency at the HPRT locus by 50–70%. In vivo, it inhibits xenograft tumor growth and prolongs survival in combination with cisplatin, validating REV1-PPI inhibition as a chemoadjuvant strategy. Its unique mechanism leverages a dynamic protein interface, achieving high specificity despite the target’s initial featureless topology.

name: 5-Benzyloxygramine
description: This compound acts as an orthosteric stabilizer of non-native PPIs in MERS-CoV N-NTD dimers. It binds at a conserved hydrophobic cavity formed by the dimer interface, simultaneously interacting with both protein partners through hydrophobic contacts. X-ray crystallography and SAXS confirmed its role in stabilizing abnormal N-NTD oligomerization, leading to antiviral effects by disrupting viral nucleocapsid function. The compound demonstrates both protein-stabilizing and antiviral activities in cellular assays.

name: Coumarin 1
description: Coumarin 1 acts as a molecular glue stabilizing the dimeric interface of immunoglobulin light chains (LCs). It binds to conserved residues at the V-domain-V-domain interface, reducing conformational excursions that lead to proteolysis and amyloidogenesis. NMR studies confirm its binding mode, showing enhanced kinetic stability of LC dimers. This compound demonstrates dose-dependent protection against Proteinase K cleavage in fluorescence polarization assays.

name: WDB002
description: WDB002 is a natural product that functions as a molecular glue by forming a ternary complex with FKBP12 and the human centrosomal protein CEP250. It targets CEP250's featureless coiled-coil domain, a previously considered "undruggable" surface. Structural studies reveal extensive protein-WDB002 and protein-protein interactions distinct from FK506- or rapamycin-induced complexes. WDB002 reprograms FKBP12 to engage flat protein surfaces, demonstrating a novel targeting modality. It disrupts CEP250 function in cells and may exhibit antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2 by interfering with CEP250-Nsp13 interactions.

name: E7820
description: E7820 is an aryl sulfonamide molecular glue that recruits RBM39 to the DCAF15 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex. It binds weakly to DCAF15 alone but synergistically stabilizes RBM39 binding through interactions with the α1 helix of RBM39's RRM2 domain. Structural studies reveal E7820 occupies a shallow pocket on DCAF15, enabling formation of a stable ternary complex that triggers RBM39 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. This mechanism underlies its anti-proliferative effects in cancer cells.

name: Tasisulam
description: Tasisulam is an aryl-sulfonamide molecular glue degrader that recruits the E3 ubiquitin ligase CRL4^DCAF15 to induce proteasomal degradation of the splicing factor RBM39. It mediates ternary complex formation between DCAF15 and RBM39's RRM2 domain with a KDapp of 3.5 µM. Unlike E7820, tasisulam exhibits weaker direct binding to DCAF15 (Ki >50 µM) but effectively promotes RBM39 degradation at low nanomolar concentrations in cells, highlighting its role as a low-affinity molecular glue.

name: Indisulam
description: Indisulam is a molecular-glue degrader that promotes the interaction between RBM39 and the DCAF15 E3 ligase, leading to RBM39 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. It binds between DCAF15 and RBM39(RRM2), coordinating additional protein-protein interactions. Structural studies reveal indisulam stabilizes a ternary complex, validating its role as a molecular glue. It exhibits potent anticancer activity by degrading RBM39, an essential splicing factor, with a KD of 109 nM for DCAF15–RBM39 binding.

name: CR-8
description: CR-8 is a molecular glue degrader that binds CDK12's ATP pocket, exposing a phenylpyridine moiety to recruit DDB1. It induces a nanomolar-affinity ternary complex (EC50 = 16 nM) by engaging DDB1's Arg928 via π–cation interactions, triggering cyclin K ubiquitination. The compound exhibits dual CDK inhibition and selective cyclin K degradation, with structural studies revealing a 2,100 Å² DDB1–CDK12 interface.

name: RBM39 Compound 9
description: RBM39 Compound 9 is an analog studied for its role in DCAF15-mediated degradation of RBM39. It likely shares structural features with indisulam, facilitating RBM39 recruitment to DCAF15. While detailed mechanistic data are limited, its inclusion suggests exploration of structure-activity relationships within the molecular-glue degrader series targeting RBM39 degradation.

name: CC-90009
description: CC-90009 is a first-in-class cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD) that selectively targets GSPT1 for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation via the CRL4CRBN complex. It exhibits potent anti-AML activity by inducing apoptosis in leukemia blasts and eliminating leukemia stem cells (LSCs). Unlike CC-885, CC-90009 shows minimal off-target degradation of other neosubstrates (e.g., IKZF1, HBS1L, CK1α). Its mechanism involves ILF2/ILF3-mediated cereblon regulation, mTOR pathway modulation, and activation of the GCN1/GCN2/ATF4 stress response. Preclinical studies demonstrate efficacy across 35 primary AML samples, including high-risk subtypes.

name: BI-3802
description: BI-3802 is a small-molecule molecular glue that binds the BTB domain of BCL6, inducing its polymerization into supramolecular filaments. This triggers SIAH1-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of BCL6, leading to potent anti-proliferative effects in DLBCL cells. Cryo-EM revealed that BI-3802 creates a composite ligand-protein interface promoting BCL6 homodimer polymerization. Unlike non-degrading inhibitors (e.g., BI-3812) or PROTACs, BI-3802 achieves BCL6 depletion comparable to genetic knockout, with high specificity observed in proteomic studies. Degradation requires the N-terminal 275 residues of BCL6 and is reversible upon competitor addition.

name: Anagrelide
description: Anagrelide is a PDE3A inhibitor clinically used for thrombocytosis treatment. It functions as a molecular glue by binding to PDE3A's catalytic pocket, enabling PDE3A to recruit and stabilize SLFN12. This interaction forms a heterotetrameric complex, blocking protein translation and inducing apoptosis. Structural studies reveal its hydrophobic moiety mediates PDE3A-SLFN12 binding. Anagrelide's apoptotic effects are abolished by PDE3 inhibitors like cilostazol, confirming PDE3A-SLFN12 dependency.

name: DNMDP
description: DNMDP is a synthetic chemical inducing apoptosis via PDE3A-SLFN12 complex formation. It binds PDE3A's catalytic domain, with its hydrophobic region extending to SLFN12, creating a molecular glue effect. Cryo-EM structures show DNMDP stabilizes the PDE3A-SLFN12 heterotetramer, inhibiting translation of anti-apoptotic proteins. Its activity is competitively inhibited by PDE3A inhibitors, highlighting the shared mechanism with other PDE3A-binding glues.

name: Nauclefine
description: Nauclefine is a natural compound acting as a molecular glue by binding PDE3A's enzymatic pocket. It promotes PDE3A-SLFN12 complex formation, stabilizing SLFN12 and triggering apoptosis through ribosomal translation blockade. Structural analysis reveals nauclefine's hydrophobic interactions bridge PDE3A and SLFN12. Like anagrelide and DNMDP, its effects are PDE3A-dependent and inhibited by competitive PDE3 inhibitors.

name: Trametinib
description: Trametinib is a clinical MEK inhibitor that uniquely engages the KSR–MEK interface through its phenyl acetamide group (section C), distinguishing it from other MEK inhibitors. It binds an allosteric pocket adjacent to ATP, with sections A and B interacting with MEK's gatekeeper residue and activation segment. Section C directly contacts KSR at the interface, exploiting conserved residues to remodel the binding pocket. This interfacial engagement enhances drug-residence time and disrupts RAF–MEK complexes, contributing to its distinct pharmacological profile.

name: Compound 2ab
description: This molecular glue compound stabilizes the noncovalent CDC34A-ubiquitin complex, inhibiting ubiquitin transfer. It was derived from isonipecotamide scaffold optimization, showing improved binding affinity compared to initial hits. The compound specifically disrupts CDC34A-dependent ubiquitination by trapping the E2~Ub thioester intermediate, as confirmed by biochemical assays and structural studies.

name: Cannabidiol
description: Cannabidiol (CBD) functions as a molecular glue in a dual-nanobody sensor system, promoting protein-protein interactions between CA14 and DB21 nanobodies. The ligand bridges these proteins by occupying a central hydrophobic pocket, enhancing their weak preexisting affinity from micromolar to nanomolar range. Structural analysis reveals CBD adopts an extended conformation, forming hydrogen bonds with CA14 while making van der Waals contacts with DB21. This system mirrors auxin and IMiD mechanisms, demonstrating CBD's role as a proximity inducer without allosteric effects.

name: IBG1
description: IBG1 is an intramolecular bivalent glue (IBG) degrader composed of the BET inhibitor JQ1 tethered to the aryl sulfonamide E7820. It induces potent BRD4 degradation (DC50 = 0.15 nM) by bridging adjacent bromodomains of BRD4 in cis, enhancing DCAF16 recruitment without direct E3 ligase binding. Thermodynamic studies reveal IBG1 strengthens the BRD4-DCAF16 interaction (Kd = 567 nM) via entropic compensation, enabling CRL4-mediated ubiquitination. Unlike PROTACs, IBG1 operates independently of DCAF15, exploiting intrinsic target-ligase affinities for selective degradation.

name: GW6471
description: GW6471 is a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-α (PPARα) antagonist that stabilizes the recruitment of the SMRT co-repressor motif. Crystal structure analysis reveals it locks the receptor's AF-2 helix in an inactive conformation, preventing transcriptional activation. This interaction facilitates histone deacetylase recruitment, leading to chromatin condensation and gene repression. GW6471's mechanism highlights its role in studying nuclear receptor-co-repressor dynamics and potential therapeutic applications in metabolic disorders.

name: Fusicoccin
description: Fusicoccin is a diterpene glycoside fungal toxin that stabilizes protein-protein interactions between 14-3-3 proteins and their client proteins. It binds at the interface of the 14-3-3/TASK-3 complex, enhancing affinity by 90-fold. Structural studies reveal its mode 3 motif specificity, promoting TASK-3 channel trafficking to the plasma membrane and increasing potassium currents in Xenopus oocytes.

name: Asoprisnil
description: Asoprisnil is a steroidal selective progesterone receptor modulator (SPRM) exhibiting mixed agonist/antagonist properties. It binds PR's ligand-binding domain, inducing a distinct conformation differing from progesterone-bound PR. Unlike RU486, it weakly recruits coactivators SRC-1/AIB1 but strongly binds corepressor NCoR. Demonstrates partial P4-like inhibition of COX-2 in ELT3 cells but fails to oppose estrogen in rat uterotrophic assays. Its unique cofactor recruitment profile underlies tissue-selective effects observed in clinical trials for uterine fibroids.

name: 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic Acid
description: This synthetic auxin analog binds directly to SCFTIR1, acting as a molecular glue to stabilize the interaction between TIR1 and Aux/IAA proteins. It promotes Aux/IAA degradation by enhancing the ubiquitin ligase activity of SCFTIR1 in a temperature-independent manner. Key findings show saturable binding at both 0.5 and 50 μM concentrations, with maximal interaction within 20-30 minutes. The continuous presence of 2,4-D is required for maintaining the TIR1-Aux/IAA complex.

name: 1-Naphthaleneacetic acid
description: A synthetic auxin that functions as a molecular glue by binding to the TIR1 receptor, facilitating Aux/IAA protein recruitment to SCFTIR1 for ubiquitination. Unlike natural auxins, it exhibits enhanced stability and potency in promoting Aux/IAA degradation. Studies demonstrate its role in auxin signaling without requiring protein modifications, directly modulating the TIR1-Aux/IAA interaction dynamics. Its efficacy parallels 2,4-D in pull-down assays.

name: Indole-3-acetic acid
description: Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) is the primary natural auxin that acts as a molecular glue between TIR1 and Aux/IAA substrates. It binds to a hydrophobic pocket in TIR1's LRR domain, enhancing substrate interaction by filling a cavity at the protein interface. Structural studies show IAA anchors at the base of the pocket, with its carboxyl group stabilized by Arg403 and the InsP6 cofactor. This binding promotes TIR1-Aux/IAA complex formation, enabling ubiquitin-mediated degradation of transcriptional repressors. IAA's planar indole ring and carboxyl side chain are critical for its auxin activity.

name: Cotylenin A (CW1)
description: Cotylenin A is a fusicoccane diterpenoid that acts as a molecular glue, stabilizing the interaction between 14-3-3 proteins and their target peptides, such as the plant H+-ATPase phosphopeptide QSYpTV. It binds at the 14-3-3/peptide interface, forming hydrophobic contacts with the diterpene ring system and accommodating the C-terminal valine. Unlike fusicoccin A, cotylenin A exhibits anti-tumor activity in human cancers, potentially due to C12 hydroxylation, which confers structural specificity for certain 14-3-3 complexes. Its aglycone retains partial biological activity.

name: BMS493
description: BMS493 is a retinoic acid receptor (RAR) inverse agonist that enhances corepressor interaction, specifically stabilizing the RAR–N-CoRNR1 complex. It induces a β-strand conformation (S3) in the RAR LBD, facilitating antiparallel β-sheet formation with N-CoRNR1. Unlike neutral antagonists, BMS493 increases corepressor recruitment and basal repression, as evidenced by structural and biochemical assays. Its mechanism involves destabilizing helix H12 while promoting a unique secondary-structure switch critical for constitutive gene silencing.

name: Epibestatin
description: Epibestatin is a dipeptide small-molecule stabilizer of the 14-3-3/PMA2 protein-protein interaction. It exhibits slow association kinetics but forms a highly stable complex (KD = 1.8 µM) by binding deeply at the interface, sharing nearly equal contact surfaces with both 14-3-3 (55%) and PMA2 (45%). Its binding mode resembles fusicoccin, filling a crevice between the proteins, resulting in strong shape-driven stabilization. Crystal structures reveal its trapping between the proteins, accounting for its slow dissociation kinetics.

name: Pyrrolidone1
description: Pyrrolidone1 is a trisubstituted pyrrolinone that stabilizes the 14-3-3/PMA2 interaction with a KD of 80 µM. It binds primarily to 14-3-3 (83% contact surface), occupying a solvent-accessible site, leading to fast association but rapid dissociation. Unlike fusicoccin, it partially fills the binding groove, suggesting potential for structural optimization. Crystal structures (3.2 Å resolution) show limited contacts with PMA2, correlating with its weaker stabilization compared to epibestatin.

name: 6,6-Dihydroxy-1-Methoxyhexan-2-One
description: This α-ketohexanone derivative features a 1-methoxy substitution and geminal diol at C-6. While not directly studied in the referenced paper, its structural features suggest potential as a scaffold for 14-3-3 protein interaction modulators. The electrophilic carbonyl at C-2 and polar diol moiety could enable covalent or polar interactions with 14-3-3 binding grooves, though specific binding data to C-RAF or 14-3-3 isoforms remain uncharacterized in this context.

name: Coronatine
description: Coronatine is a bacterial phytotoxin that structurally and functionally mimics the bioactive jasmonate hormone (3R,7S)-JA-Ile. It binds with high affinity (Kd = 48–68 nM) to the COI1–JAZ co-receptor complex, triggering JAZ degradation and jasmonate signaling. Coronatine competes with JA-Ile for COI1–JAZ binding, demonstrating its role as a molecular glue stabilizing the ternary complex. Its mechanism involves interaction with the JAZ degron sequence and inositol pentakisphosphate, a critical co-receptor component.

name: (3R,7S)-JA-L-Ile
description: (3R,7S)-JA-L-Ile is the bioactive jasmonate hormone conjugate that binds the COI1–JAZ co-receptor with high specificity (Ki = 1.8 µM). It induces JAZ degradation via SCFCOI1-mediated ubiquitylation, releasing MYC2 transcription factors. The hormone’s binding requires a bipartite JAZ degron and inositol pentakisphosphate, forming a ternary complex. The (3R,7S) stereoisomer exhibits significantly higher activity than the (3R,7R) isomer, highlighting stereochemical specificity in receptor recognition.

name: Cotylenin A (CW7)
description: Cotylenin A (CW7) is a fusicoccane derivative with demonstrated activity in stabilizing 14-3-3 protein interactions. It shares structural similarities with fusicoccin A but exhibits distinct binding properties. Its mechanism involves enhancing 14-3-3/client protein complexes, though its specific effects on TASK-3 channels remain less characterized compared to FC-THF.

name: Fusicoccin A aglycone
description: Fusicoccin A aglycone is the non-glycosylated core structure of fusicoccin A. It retains the ability to modulate 14-3-3 protein interactions but with reduced potency compared to the glycosylated form. Its mechanism involves binding to the 14-3-3/TASK-3 interface, though its stabilizing effects are less pronounced.

name: Fusicoccin J aglycone
description: Fusicoccin J aglycone is a structural analog of fusicoccin A aglycone with modifications in the diterpene scaffold. It exhibits weaker binding to 14-3-3/TASK-3 complexes, highlighting the importance of specific functional groups for molecular glue activity. Its effects on channel trafficking are less significant than fusicoccin A.

name: Fusicoccin A-THF
description: Fusicoccin A-THF (FC-THF) is a semisynthetic fusicoccane derivative designed to target the 14-3-3/TASK-3 interaction. It stabilizes the complex with a 19-fold increased affinity, as shown by crystallography. FC-THF enhances TASK-3 surface expression and potassium currents in Xenopus oocytes, demonstrating its potential as a PPI stabilizer.

name: Cotylenol
description: Cotylenol is a fusicoccane alcohol derivative lacking the glycoside moiety. It shows moderate activity in stabilizing 14-3-3 protein interactions but is less effective than fusicoccin A. Its mechanism involves binding to the 14-3-3 groove, though its impact on TASK-3 channel function is limited.

name: Fusicoccin H
description: Fusicoccin H is a naturally occurring fusicoccane with structural variations in the diterpene core. It exhibits weaker binding to 14-3-3/TASK-3 complexes compared to fusicoccin A, emphasizing the role of specific substituents in molecular glue efficacy. Its functional effects on channel trafficking are minimal.

name: 16-O-Me-FC-H
description: 16-O-Me-FC-H is a methylated derivative of fusicoccin H, with altered hydrophobicity and binding properties. It shows reduced activity in stabilizing 14-3-3/TASK-3 interactions, underscoring the sensitivity of fusicoccane derivatives to structural modifications. Its impact on potassium channel expression is negligible.

name: Cotylenin-A (CN-A)
description: CN-A is a natural product molecular glue that selectively stabilizes the inhibitory interaction between C-RAF (phosphorylated at Ser233/Ser259) and 14-3-3ζ, reducing the dissociation constant 17-fold (KD = 20 nM). Structural analysis reveals CN-A binds at the C-RAF/14-3-3 interface, with specificity conferred by steric exclusion from the activating pSer621 site. While inactive alone in RAS-mutant models, CN-A synergizes with anti-EGFR antibodies to suppress tumor growth by attenuating ERK activation paradoxically induced by CN-A monotherapy.

name: Compound 24
description: Compound 24 is a small-molecule stabilizer of the PfAldolase-TRAP interaction in Plasmodium falciparum. It inhibits parasite motility and invasion by strengthening the protein-protein interface, preventing TRAP dissociation and glideosome recycling. X-ray crystallography confirms its binding at the PfAldolase-TRAP interface, occluding the catalytic site. In vitro assays demonstrate 95% reduction in hepatocyte invasion. This molecular glue mechanism represents a novel strategy targeting previously "undruggable" glideosome dynamics.

name: ISIR-005
description: ISIR-005 is a semi-synthetic natural product derivative that stabilizes the 14-3-3/Gab2 protein-protein interaction (PPI). It binds at the rim-of-the-interface of the 14-3-3/Gab2pT391 complex, occupying a pre-formed pocket near the Gab2pT391 site. Crystal structures reveal it selectively stabilizes Gab2pT391 binding without affecting the Gab2pS210 motif. This molecular glue demonstrates druggability of the 14-3-3/Gab2 interface, offering potential for PPI stabilizer development in cancer therapeutics.

name: CLR01
description: CLR01 is a molecular tweezer that stabilizes protein-protein interactions by acting as a supramolecular "Janus" ligand. It simultaneously binds to a flexible peptidic recognition motif (R208 of Cdc25CpS216) and the structured 14-3-3ζ protein, filling a gap in the interface. This dual binding enhances the apparent affinity by ~20-fold and induces disorder-to-order transition in the intrinsically disordered Cdc25C partner. Crystal structures confirm its unique ability to "freeze" conformational states while engaging both polar (lysine/arginine) and nonpolar interactions.

name: FC-NAc
description: FC-NAc is a semisynthetic fusicoccane derivative designed to enhance 14-3-3 protein-protein interaction (PPI) stabilization. It replaces the 19-acetoxy group of fusicoccin-A with an acetamide, introducing an additional hydrogen-bond donor. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed its stable interaction with Asp215 of 14-3-3, forming a persistent hydrogen bond (97.1% of frames). This modification significantly increased potency compared to the parent compound, demonstrating the utility of rational design for PPI stabilizers. FC-NAc also exhibited enhanced cellular activity, validating its potential as a tool compound or therapeutic candidate.

name: S-Pomalidomide
description: S-Pomalidomide is a cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD) that induces CRL4CRBN-mediated degradation of neosubstrates, including SALL4. It binds cereblon with high affinity, recruiting SALL4 via its ZF2 β-hairpin degron featuring a critical glycine (G416). Structural studies reveal a 15° rotation in SALL4 binding compared to Ikaros, driven by steric clashes involving H417. This compound exhibits greater SALL4 degradation potency than thalidomide, highlighting its role in teratogenicity while retaining therapeutic potential for hematological malignancies.

name: NRX-2776
description: NRX-2776 is a small molecular glue enhancer of the β-Catenin/β-TrCP interaction. It binds at the PPI interface, stabilizing the complex between mutant β-Catenin (pSer33/Ser37) and β-TrCP. This compound enhances ubiquitylation of β-Catenin in vitro and promotes degradation of engineered mutant β-Catenin in cellular systems. Its mechanism involves optimizing contacts with both substrate and ligase, distinct from PROTACs.

name: NRX-103094
description: NRX-103094 functions as a molecular glue by inserting into the β-Catenin/β-TrCP interface, restoring binding affinity for Ser37-mutant β-Catenin. It demonstrates potent enhancement of ubiquitylation in biochemical assays and induces cellular degradation of mutant β-Catenin. The compound’s drug-like properties circumvent limitations of bifunctional degraders.

name: NRX-2663
description: NRX-2663 is a rationally designed small molecule that stabilizes the β-Catenin/β-TrCP complex. It targets the phosphodegron-binding pocket of β-TrCP, compensating for Ser37 mutations in β-Catenin. Cellular assays confirm its ability to degrade engineered mutant β-Catenin, validating its molecular glue mechanism.

name: NRX-1933
description: NRX-1933 enhances the interaction between β-TrCP and phosphodeficient β-Catenin (pSer33/Ser37) by acting as a molecular glue. It exhibits nanomolar affinity in FP assays and promotes proteasomal degradation of mutant β-Catenin in cells. Its structure optimizes dual contacts with ligase and substrate.

name: FC-NCPC
description: FC-NCPC is a semisynthetic 19-amide derivative of fusicoccin-A (FC-A) with enhanced binding affinity for 14-3-3 protein complexes. It features an N-cyclopropylcarbonyl substitution at position 19, forming an additional hydrogen bond with Asp215 in the 14-3-3 groove. FC-NCPC exhibits dual functionality as a molecular glue, both stabilizing and competitively inhibiting specific 14-3-3 protein-protein interactions (PPIs). In neuronal assays, it demonstrates potent neurite outgrowth stimulation (EC50 ~single-digit μM) and enhances axon regeneration in vitro, likely through polypharmacological modulation of Rap1 signaling network components.

name: Pyrrolidone1 (Different Chirality)
description: Pyrrolidone1 exhibits chirality-dependent PPI stabilization effects on the 14-3-3/ERα(pT594) complex. The racemic mixture (rac-2) shows weak stabilization (1.4-fold at 200 μM), while enantiopure forms display distinct potencies in FP assays. NMR studies reveal binding to the FC pocket of 14-3-3, with key interactions involving residues lining this interface. The stereochemistry significantly influences the bioactive conformation and stabilization efficacy, suggesting chirality as a critical factor for molecular glue development targeting this PPI.

name: Pyrrolidone1 derivative
description: This derivative class demonstrates metal-ion-dependent 14-3-3 PPI stabilization, with Mg²⁺ chelation enhancing potency up to 100-fold. X-ray crystallography revealed an unexpected ligand-chelated Mg²⁺ interaction, inducing a bioactive conformation that stabilizes the ternary complex. The chelation-controlled mechanism bypasses traditional PAINS liabilities, offering a novel strategy for drug-like PPI stabilizers. Optimized derivatives mimic this effect via intramolecular hydrogen bonds, achieving natural product-level potency (low μM) while maintaining selectivity.

name: 16-OMe-Fusicoccin H
description: 16-OMe-Fusicoccin H is a fusicoccane diterpene glycoside that stabilizes the interaction between CaMKK2 and 14-3-3γ by binding at their interface. It enhances the affinity of phosphorylated CaMKK2 for 14-3-3γ, prolonging the kinase's inhibited state. Structural analysis reveals its C-terminal interactions within the 14-3-3 binding groove contribute to stabilization potency. This compound demonstrates weaker effects compared to Fusicoccin A but retains molecular glue properties by filling gaps in the protein-protein interaction interface.

name: Compound 3
description: Compound 3 is a rationally optimized phenylphosphonate-based molecular glue that selectively stabilizes the 14-3-3β/ChREBP protein-protein interaction (PPI). Its structure features a phenethylamide-linked phenylphosphonate core, enabling simultaneous engagement with both 14-3-3β (via residues K51, R58, R129, and Y130 in the phospho-accepting pocket) and ChREBP (via R128 and W127), forming a ternary complex. Key structural determinants include the ethyl linker length (n=2), which positions the second phenyl ring to occupy a composite hydrophobic interface formed by ChREBP’s I120 and 14-3-3β’s I219/L222/L174. This unique binding mode, elucidated by X-ray crystallography (PDB: 6YGJ), contrasts with shorter-linker analogs (e.g., 12) that act as inhibitors by binding only 14-3-3β. Compound 3 enhances the 14-3-3β/ChREBP affinity by 14-fold (EC50= 5.2 µM) with negligible inhibition of other 14-3-3/client complexes (e.g., TAZ, ERα, p53), demonstrating exceptional selectivity and cooperative stabilization.

name: S-Thalidomide
description: (S)-Thalidomide is the active enantiomer that binds cereblon (CRBN) to form the CRL4CRBN E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, inducing proteasomal degradation of neosubstrates like IKZF1/3 and SALL4. Its (S)-configuration enables stronger CRBN binding than the (R)-enantiomer, driving selective recruitment of C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factors. Structural studies show its glutarimide ring anchors at the CRBN-SALL4 interface, with the phthalimide moiety positioned to influence substrate specificity.

name: (S)-5-hydroxythalidomide
description: (S)-5-Hydroxythalidomide, a primary thalidomide metabolite, exhibits enhanced SALL4 degradation over its parent compound due to an additional hydroxy group at the phthalimide C5 position. This modification strengthens CRBN binding and alters neosubstrate selectivity by forming a hydrogen bond with CRBN's W400, preferentially recruiting SALL4 over IKZF1/3. Crystal structures reveal its β-hairpin interaction defines C2H2 ZF-type substrate specificity, linking metabolism to teratogenic effects.

name: ALV1
description: ALV1 is an anilinomaleimide-based molecular glue degrader that recruits CRBN to induce proteasomal degradation of both Helios (IKZF2) and Ikaros (IKZF1). It exhibits stronger CRBN binding (IC50 = 0.55 µM) and CRBN-Helios dimerization (Emax = 2.26 AU) than lenalidomide but weaker than CC-885. Unlike CC-885, ALV1 spares GSPT1, reducing cytotoxicity. Its flexible core accommodates Helios' histidine residue, enabling dual degradation while maintaining selectivity among IKZF family members.

name: DKY709
description: DKY709 is a selective molecular glue degrader targeting IKZF2 (Helios) while sparing IKZF1/3. It recruits IKZF2 to the CRBN E3 ligase, inducing proteasomal degradation. Structural analysis of the DDB1:CRBN:DKY709:IKZF2(ZF2) complex rationalizes its selectivity. DKY709 reduces Treg suppression in vitro and degrades IKZF2 in preclinical models, including monkeys and humans. Its mechanism enhances anti-tumor immunity by destabilizing Treg function, making it a clinical candidate for cancer immunotherapy.

name: Compound 8
description: Compound 8 acts as a molecular glue stabilizing the 14-3-3σ/C-RAF phosphopeptide interaction. It binds reversibly to C38 via disulfide tethering, enhancing the PPI affinity by up to 430-fold. Structural analysis reveals its selective engagement with the composite interface formed by 14-3-3σ and the linear C-RAF peptide motif. This fragment shows minimal stabilization for other client peptides, demonstrating high selectivity for the C-RAF interaction.

name: Compound 7
description: Compound 7 is a disulfide-tethered fragment that selectively stabilizes the 14-3-3σ/FOXO1 phosphopeptide complex. It exhibits cooperative binding with the curved FOXO1 peptide motif, increasing PPI affinity by 120-fold. Crystallography confirms its productive interactions with both 14-3-3σ and the tryptophan residue at the +1 position of FOXO1. The fragment shows no significant stabilization of other client peptides.

name: Compound 2
description: Compound 2 non-selectively stabilizes multiple 14-3-3σ/client interactions, including ERα and C-RAF. It engages C38 via disulfide exchange but lacks pronounced selectivity due to its ability to adapt to diverse peptide conformations. Functional assays show moderate affinity enhancements (20–50-fold) across targets. Structural data suggest its flexibility enables binding to both truncated and linear peptide motifs.

name: Compound 3
description: Compound 3 is a selective stabilizer of the 14-3-3σ/ERα interaction, enhancing binding affinity by 40-fold. It targets the composite interface formed by the C-terminal ERα phosphopeptide and 14-3-3σ. The fragment's covalent attachment to C38 is reinforced by hydrophobic interactions with the valine residue at the +1 position of ERα.

name: Compound 5
description: Compound 5 demonstrates selective stabilization of the 14-3-3σ/USP8 phosphopeptide complex. It binds C38 and extends into the composite pocket formed by the linear USP8 peptide, increasing PPI affinity by 90-fold. The fragment's selectivity arises from its complementarity to the serine residue at the +1 position of USP8.

name: Compound 1
description: Compound 1 is a non-selective molecular glue that stabilizes both 14-3-3σ/ERα and 14-3-3σ/FOXO1 interactions. It engages C38 and adapts to either truncated (ERα) or curved (FOXO1) peptide motifs, enhancing affinities by 30–60-fold. Structural analysis reveals its promiscuity stems from a flexible scaffold that accommodates diverse peptide conformations.

name: CC-92480 (mezigdomide)
description: CC-92480 is a cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD) designed for efficient and rapid degradation of Ikaros (IKZF1) and Aiolos (IKZF3). It exhibits potent antiproliferative activity in lenalidomide-resistant multiple myeloma (MM) cells while maintaining selectivity against normal PBMCs. Its optimized degradation kinetics and efficiency translate to strong apoptosis induction, making it the first CELMoD specifically developed for rapid protein degradation to enter clinical trials for relapsed/refractory MM.

name: CC-220 (iberdomide)
description: CC-220 is a cereblon modulator with enhanced binding affinity (IC50 = 60 nM) compared to lenalidomide/pomalidomide. It induces potent degradation of Ikaros (EC50 = 1 nM) and Aiolos (EC50 = 0.5 nM) via CRL4-CRBN E3 ligase recruitment. Structural analysis reveals additional contacts with cereblon's surface, correlating with improved substrate depletion. Unlike lenalidomide, it does not degrade CK1α or GSPT1, demonstrating substrate selectivity. Currently in clinical trials for multiple myeloma and lupus.

name: RMC-7977
description: RMC-7977 is a reversible tri-complex inhibitor that recruits cyclophilin A (CYPA) to active-state RAS mutants, exhibiting mutation-specific effects. It demonstrates potent stimulation of GTP hydrolysis in G12X KRAS mutants (particularly G12D, G12A, G12S, G12V, G12C, and G12R) but minimal activity against Q61X or A59T mutants. The drug-bound CYPA complex modulates switch II residues to facilitate γ-phosphate cleavage. RMC-7977 also disrupts effector binding (e.g., CRAF) while showing limited impact on SOS1-mediated nucleotide exchange. Its hydrolysis-enhancing activity inversely correlates with CYPA binding stability across RAS isoforms.

name: NK7-288
description: NK7-288 is a cereblon (CRBN)-targeting molecular glue degrader that induces NEK7 degradation. It demonstrates partial inhibition of NLRP3 inflammasome-dependent IL-1β release in human primary monocytes, though with variable efficacy across donors. Unlike many CRBN degraders, it exhibits cross-species activity, degrading NEK7 in murine cells. Its mechanism involves exploiting NEK7's glycine beta hairpin loop degron for CRBN-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.

name: NK7-147
description: NK7-147 is a CRBN-dependent molecular glue degrader selective for NEK7. It achieves potent NEK7 degradation in human primary monocytes and PBMCs but shows context-dependent NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition, with incomplete IL-1β suppression. Structural analysis suggests it stabilizes the CRBN-NEK7 interaction via the glycine beta hairpin degron. Its murine activity distinguishes it from typical CRBN degraders.

name: NK7-902
description: NK7-902 is a lead CRBN molecular glue degrader that fully depletes NEK7 in human and non-human primate cells. Despite robust NEK7 degradation, it only transiently inhibits NLRP3-driven IL-1β in primates, suggesting NEK7's non-essential role in inflammasome activation. It retains activity in murine systems, effectively suppressing IL-1β in a CAPS model, highlighting species-specific mechanistic differences.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 1
description: This glutarimide-based molecular glue degrader demonstrates CRBN-dependent dual degradation of WEE1 and CK1α, with an EC50 of 12 nM in MOLT-4 cells. It shows stronger WEE1 degradation compared to CK1α and exhibits antiproliferative effects. Proteomics and Western blotting confirm its selectivity, with minimal off-target degradation of other CRBN neo-substrates like IKZF1/2 or GSPT1 at 5-hour treatment.

name: SJ3149
description: SJ3149 is a selective and potent molecular glue degrader of CK1α, developed through structure-guided SAR optimization of SJ7095. It induces targeted proteolysis by forming a ternary complex with CRBN and CK1α, as evidenced by its co-crystal structure with CK1α+CRBN+DDB1. SJ3149 exhibits broad antiproliferative activity across 115 cancer cell lines, with a profile statistically correlated to MDM2 inhibitor Nutlin-3a. Its improved degradation properties and selectivity make it a promising candidate for hematological and solid tumor therapies.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 1-Me
description: A methylated derivative of Compound 1, this molecular glue maintains CRBN-mediated degradation of WEE1 and CK1α. Its modified structure may influence binding kinetics or selectivity, though detailed mechanistic data are not provided in the study.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 2
description: The most potent hit (EC50 = 5 nM), this compound induces CRBN- and proteasome-dependent degradation of both WEE1 and CK1α in MOLT-4 cells. Unlike other derivatives, it shows no off-target degradation of IKZF1/2 or GSPT1 at 5 hours. MLN4924 pretreatment rescues degradation, confirming Cullin ligase dependency.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 3
description: Exhibiting an EC50 of 139 nM, this degrader strongly targets WEE1 over CK1α. It shows modest GSPT1 degradation, potentially contributing to its antiproliferative effects. CRBN dependency is validated via knockout cell experiments.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 4
description: A synthetic analog from the GBB-derived library, this compound's degradation profile aligns with the HRZ-1 scaffold. It requires further characterization to elucidate its selectivity and potency relative to other derivatives.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 5
description: This member of the HRZ-1 series demonstrates CRBN-dependent degradation activity. Structural modifications likely fine-tune its interaction with the WEE1 β-hairpin region, though specific SAR data are not detailed.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 6
description: Part of the multicomponent reaction library, this compound's glutarimide core facilitates CRBN engagement. Its degradation efficiency and selectivity for WEE1/CK1α warrant further optimization.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 7
description: A synthetic derivative designed to explore SAR around the HRZ-1 scaffold. Its mechanism involves stabilizing the CRBN-WEE1/CK1α ternary complex, leading to proteasomal degradation.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 8
description: This compound's antiproliferative effects in MOLT-4 cells suggest CRBN-mediated degradation activity. Structural features may influence its binding to the kinase domain of WEE1.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 9
description: A modularly synthesized degrader from the GBB reaction, its compact structure aligns with molecular glue properties. Further studies are needed to quantify its degradation kinetics.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 10
description: Exhibits CRBN-dependent protein degradation, likely through the conserved glutarimide-binding pocket. Its selectivity profile remains under investigation relative to other HRZ-1 derivatives.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 11
description: Designed to probe the chemical space around the HRZ-1 core, this compound's efficacy in degrading WEE1/CK1α is modulated by its heterocyclic substitutions.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 12
description: A candidate from the combinatorial library, its degradation mechanism involves ubiquitination via CRL4CRBN. Structural insights suggest interactions with WEE1's β-hairpin region.

name: WEE1/CK1α Dual Degrader Compound 13
description: This derivative underscores the versatility of the HRZ-1 scaffold in targeting kinases. Its CRBN-dependent activity and potential therapeutic relevance require further validation.

name: YB-3-17
description: YB-3-17 is a bifunctional small molecule combining mTOR inhibition with GSPT1 degradation. It features a piperidine-substituted tetrahydropyrrole core and cyclohexane linker, optimizing conformational flexibility and stability. YB-3-17 demonstrates robust mTOR kinase inhibition (IC50 < 100 nM) and selective GSPT1 degradation (DC50 ~50 nM) in glioblastoma cells. RNA-seq analysis confirms its superior efficacy over mTOR inhibitor monotherapy, disrupting translation via dual mechanisms. In vivo, it exhibits potent antitumor activity with reduced off-target effects, validating the dual-target, dual-mechanism strategy for glioblastoma treatment.

name: ZZ1-SO2H
description: ZZ1-SO2H is a negatively charged molecular glue degrader (c-Glue) derived from the prodrug ZZ1, featuring an unmasked sulfinic acid moiety. It selectively targets BET-family proteins (BRD3/4) by recruiting the GID/CTLH ubiquitin ligase complex via electrostatic interactions with the basic pocket of YPEL5, a CRBN homolog. This compound demonstrates YPEL5-dependent degradation, revealing a novel mechanism for exploiting charged degron recognition. Its discovery highlights the potential of sulfinic acid-based glues to engage non-Cullin E3 ligases.

name: ZZ2-SO2H
description: ZZ2-SO2H is a rationally optimized c-Glue derived from ZZ1-SO2H, retaining the sulfinic acid group for YPEL5 binding. It exhibits enhanced degradation efficiency of BRD4 by leveraging the GID/CTLH complex. The compound validates the chemocentric strategy for charged glue discovery, emphasizing electrostatic-driven proximity induction. Structural insights reveal YPEL5's role in recruiting neosubstrates, expanding degradable target space.

name: CIP-1
description: CIP-1 is a proximity-inducing small molecule featuring a VHL-targeting ligand connected to a bromodomain-binding moiety via a C15 linker. It demonstrated high enrichment in BRD4 (+) VHL screens, indicating stable ternary complex formation with VHL and BRD4BD1. The compound's molecular glue properties were confirmed through cellular degradation assays and structural studies, showing cooperative binding between target and presenter proteins.

name: CIP-2
description: CIP-2 contains a VHL-binding motif linked to a diverse triazine-based warhead through connector C14. It exhibited preferential enrichment in BRD4 (+) VHL screens, suggesting its role in inducing neo-PPIs. Cellular validation confirmed its ability to promote BRD4 degradation via VHL recruitment.

name: CIP-3
description: CIP-3 incorporates BB2-109 as its diversity element, paired with the C15 connector. It showed significant enrichment in both BRD4 (±) VHL screens, highlighting its dual-binding capability. Structural analysis revealed optimal positioning for ternary complex stabilization.

name: CIP-4
description: CIP-4 features BB3-114 as its triazine substituent, demonstrating strong cooperative binding in the presence of VHL. Its enrichment profile suggests efficient induction of BRD4-VHL proximity, leading to targeted protein degradation in cellular assays.

name: CIP-5
description: CIP-5 utilizes a truncated C14 linker with BB2-109, showing moderate enrichment in BRD4 (+) VHL screens. While less potent than C15 analogs, it retains molecular glue activity, confirming linker length SAR for ternary complex formation.

name: CIP-6
description: CIP-6 combines the C15 connector with a distinct triazine warhead, exhibiting selective enrichment in VHL-dependent screens. Cellular studies validated its proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC)-like mechanism, degrading BRD4 via the ubiquitin-proteasome system.

name: CIP-7
description: CIP-7 employs a non-preferred connector but retains measurable enrichment in BRD4 (+) VHL screens. Its weaker activity underscores the critical role of linker optimization in proximity-inducing molecule design.

name: CIP-8
description: CIP-8 integrates BB3-114 with a suboptimal linker, resulting in reduced ternary complex stability. Its partial activity highlights the interplay between connector flexibility and warhead specificity in molecular glue efficacy.

name: CIP-9
description: CIP-9 features an alternative triazine building block, showing modest enrichment in BRD4 (−) VHL screens but limited VHL-dependent activity. This suggests its primary role as a monovalent binder rather than a proximity inducer.

name: CIP-10
description: CIP-10 pairs BB2-109 with a rigid aromatic connector, exhibiting unique enrichment patterns. While less efficient than flexible linkers, it induced detectable BRD4 degradation, supporting diverse linker chemotypes for CIP discovery.

name: CIP-11
description: CIP-11’s design diverges from top-performing analogs, using a bulky cycle 3 substituent. Its low enrichment in BRD4 (+) VHL screens emphasizes steric constraints in ternary complex formation.

name: CIP-12
description: CIP-12 incorporates a polar connector, demonstrating solvent-exposed compatibility in ternary complexes. Its moderate activity suggests potential for targeting alternative E3 ligases or bromodomains.

name: CIP-13
description: CIP-13 combines C15 with a heterocyclic warhead, showing cooperative binding but lower cellular potency. Structural insights revealed suboptimal orientation for ubiquitination, informing future design iterations.

name: CIP-14
description: CIP-14’s asymmetric linker design yielded intermediate enrichment, bridging VHL and BRD4BD1 without steric clashes. Its balanced profile supports the exploration of non-linear connectors in CIPs.

name: CIP-15
description: CIP-15, a C15-linked analog with a hydrophobic warhead, achieved high cellular degradation efficacy. Crystal structures confirmed its role in stabilizing the BRD4-VHL interface, validating the DEL screening approach.

name: CIP-16
description: CIP-16’s shorter linker compromised ternary complex stability, underscoring the 15-atom spacer’s superiority. Its weak activity refined SAR for connector length in bifunctional degraders.

name: CIP-17
description: CIP-17 features a cyclic connector, exhibiting unique binding kinetics. While enrichment was lower than linear analogs, it expanded the chemical space for proximity-inducing scaffolds.

name: CIP-18
description: CIP-18’s flexible polyethylene glycol linker showed promiscuous binding but poor degradation, highlighting the need for rigidified designs to optimize ternary complex lifetimes.

name: CIP-19
description: CIP-19 integrates a sulfonamide warhead, demonstrating VHL-dependent BRD4 engagement. Its moderate enrichment suggests potential for targeting non-bromodomain proteins.

name: CIP-20
description: CIP-20’s sterically hindered connector reduced BRD4 binding, emphasizing the delicate balance between linker bulk and target accessibility in molecular glues.

name: CIP-21
description: CIP-21, a C14-linked variant with BB3-114, mirrored top performers but with reduced potency. Its consistent SAR supports the generality of preferred building blocks across linkers.

name: CIP-22
description: CIP-22’s zwitterionic warhead disrupted ternary complex formation, revealing electrostatic incompatibilities in the BRD4-VHL interface.

name: CIP-23
description: CIP-23, a C15-BB2-109 hybrid, exhibited robust degradation activity, cementing this combination as a privileged scaffold for VHL-recruiting degraders. Structural data confirmed its optimal binding pose.

name: dCeMM3
description: dCeMM3 is a cryptic cyclin K degrader identified through systematic screening. It stabilizes CDK12–DDB1 interactions by binding CDK12's hinge region while engaging DDB1's interfacial residues, particularly Arg928. Cellular assays confirm cyclin K depletion independent of pronounced kinase inhibition, highlighting its glue-specific mechanism.

name: NRX-1532
description: NRX-1532 is a potent molecular glue that rescues β-TrCP binding to Ser37-mutant β-Catenin. Biochemical studies show it restores ubiquitylation activity, while cellular models demonstrate degradation of stabilized β-Catenin. The compound’s small size and efficiency distinguish it from PROTACs.

name: NRX-103095
description: NRX-103095 binds cooperatively with β-Catenin and β-TrCP, acting as a PPI enhancer. It specifically targets the pSer33/Ser37 mutant, improving ligase engagement and degradation. Its mechanism involves extending the hydrophobic interface between substrate and ligase.

name: NRX-252114
description: NRX-252114 is a optimized molecular glue that potentiates β-TrCP-mediated ubiquitylation of phosphodeficient β-Catenin. It exhibits superior cellular activity in degrading mutant β-Catenin, with structural features tailored to the ligase-substrate interface.

name: NRX-252262
description: NRX-252262 enhances β-Catenin degradation by bridging β-TrCP and mutant β-Catenin (pSer33/Ser37). Its design leverages structure-guided optimization to maximize interactions with both proteins, resulting in efficient cellular degradation.

name: MMH2
description: MMH2 is a covalent molecular glue degrader derived from JQ1, targeting BRD4BD2 via DCAF16 recruitment. It employs template-assisted covalent modification to alkylate DCAF16Cys58, stabilizing the BRD4–degrader–DCAF16 ternary complex and inducing proteasomal degradation. Biochemical assays confirm its selectivity for BRD4BD2 over BRD4BD1, with CRISPR screens validating DCAF16 dependency. MMH2's acrolein warhead enhances degradation efficacy compared to non-covalent analogs, demonstrating the utility of covalent mechanisms in molecular glue design.

name: MMH1
description: MMH1 is a JQ1-based covalent molecular glue that recruits DCAF16 to BRD4BD2, facilitating targeted degradation. Its mechanism involves structural pre-organization between DCAF16 and BRD4BD2, enabling precise covalent modification of DCAF16Cys58. Proteomic analyses reveal BRD4-specific degradation, while genetic knockout studies confirm DCAF16 as essential for activity. MMH1's reactive group optimizes ternary complex stability, highlighting the role of covalent anchoring in proximity-driven pharmacology.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound L1
description: 4-Imidazole-benzaldehyde fragment forming reversible aldimine bonds with Lys122 of 14-3-3σ. Stabilizes the p65/14-3-3 interaction via hydrophobic contacts with Ile+1 of p65, as evidenced by X-ray crystallography (PDB 6YP2). Serves as a foundational fragment for imine-tethering approaches targeting 14-3-3 hub protein interfaces.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound L2
description: L2 (4-(4-chloro-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) stabilizes the Pin1/14-3-3 complex with a CC₅₀ of 423 µM and a stabilization factor (SF) of 1.3. It induces a ~90° conformational shift in Trp+1 of Pin1, enabling π-π stacking interactions (PDB: 7AXN). This fragment serves as a key starting point for optimization due to its halogen-driven binding in the P1 subpocket.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound L3
description: L3 (4-(5-bromo-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) exhibits moderate stabilization (CC₅₀ = 480 µM, SF = 2.4) via imine tethering to Lys122. The crystal structure (PDB: 7AYF) reveals hydrophobic contacts in the P2 subpocket. Its bromine substitution probes alternative binding regions, informing subsequent SAR studies for selective PPI enhancement.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 1
description: Compound 1 (3-bromo-4-(1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) shows no stabilization activity (CC₅₀ >1,000 µM), contrasting with L2. The shift of bromine to the 3-position abolishes binding potency, highlighting the critical role of halogen placement in the P1 subpocket for cooperative ternary complex formation.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 2
description: Compound 2 (2-chloro-4-(1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) demonstrates improved stabilization (CC₅₀ = 153 µM, SF = 2.6) compared to L2. The 2-chloro substitution optimizes hydrophobic contacts with Asn42, Val46, and Phe119 of 14-3-3, validating the strategic exploration of halogen positioning for affinity enhancement.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 3
description: Compound 3 (2-bromo-4-(1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) achieves a CC₅₀ of 61 µM and SF of 3.5. Structural analysis (PDB: 7NIG) confirms deeper engagement in the P1 pocket via bromine interactions. This fragment establishes the significance of 2-halogen substitutions for maximizing hydrophobic complementarity.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 4
description: Compound 4 (4-(4-methyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) shows no stabilization (CC₅₀ >1,000 µM). Methylation at the imidazole 4-position fails to engage the P3 subpocket (Leu218/Ile219), as observed in low-occupancy electron density (PDB: 7NRK), indicating steric incompatibility for cooperative binding.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 5
description: Compound 5 (4-(5-methyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) exhibits no activity (CC₅₀ >1,000 µM). The 5-methyl group disrupts binding at the P2 pocket (Ile168/Asn42), underscoring the sensitivity of the composite interface to small steric perturbations in this region.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 6
description: Compound 6 (4-(4-(trifluoromethyl)-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) is inactive (CC₅₀ >1,000 µM) despite structural data (PDB: 7NJ6) showing weak interactions with Asp215 in the P3 pocket. The trifluoromethyl group's size and polarity preclude productive cooperativity with Pin1.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 7
description: Compound 7 (4-(1H-benzo[d]imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) displays no stabilization (CC₅₀ >1,000 µM). The benzimidazole moiety engages Leu218/Ile219 (PDB: 7NJ8) but induces excessive bulk, distorting the Trp+1 orientation and disrupting π-stacking essential for ternary complex stability.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 8
description: Compound 8 (1-(4-formylphenyl)-1H-imidazole-2-carboxylic acid) is inactive (CC₅₀ >1,000 µM). The carboxylic acid group at the imidazole 2-position creates electrostatic repulsion in the hydrophobic P2 pocket, eliminating potential hydrogen-bonding benefits for PPI stabilization.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 9
description: Compound 9 (4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) exhibits marginal activity (CC₅₀ >500 µM). The 2-phenyl group samples the P2 pocket but shows rotational freedom in crystallography (PDB: 7NJA), limiting productive interactions. This informed rigidification strategies in later analogs.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 10
description: Compound 10 (2-chloro-4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) shows moderate stabilization (CC₅₀ = 166 µM, SF = 3.6). The 2-chloro/2-phenyl combination probes P1 and P2 pockets but suffers from conformational flexibility, as evidenced by suboptimal binding pose consolidation (PDB: 7BDP).

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 11
description: Compound 11 (3-chloro-4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) is inactive (CC₅₀ >500 µM). Meta-chloro substitution disrupts the vector for Lys122 tethering and P1 engagement, confirming the requirement for ortho-halogen placement to access the hydrophobic subpocket.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 12
description: Compound 12 (3-bromo-4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) shows no activity (CC₅₀ >500 µM). Analogous to compound 11, the 3-bromo position fails to engage the P1 subpocket, reinforcing the spatial constraints for productive fragment binding.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 13
description: Compound 13 (2-bromo-4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) achieves significant stabilization (CC₅₀ = 101 µM, SF = 10.8). It induces a water-mediated hydrogen bond between Pin1's Gln+3 and 14-3-3's Asn42 (PDB: 7BDT). The α-factor of ~60 confirms cooperative complex formation, though high-concentration aggregation limits efficacy.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 14
description: Compound 14 (4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)-2-(trifluoromethyl)benzaldehyde) has moderate activity (CC₅₀ = 306 µM, SF = 1.2). The 2-CF₃ group partially occupies a deep pocket near Cys38/Arg41 (PDB: 7AZ1) but insufficiently locks the ligand orientation, resulting in suboptimal cooperativity.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 15
description: Compound 15 (4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)-3-(trifluoromethyl)benzaldehyde) is inactive (CC₅₀ >500 µM). Meta-trifluoromethyl placement disrupts the aldehyde-Lys122 geometry, preventing imine formation and underscoring the sensitivity of covalent anchor positioning.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 16
description: Compound 16 (2-methoxy-4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) causes assay interference due to autofluorescence (ex/em scans). This optical artifact invalidates its FA-based evaluation, highlighting the importance of orthogonal validation for fluorescent compounds.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 17
description: Compound 17 (3-methoxy-4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) exhibits autofluorescence, complicating FA interpretation. Its methoxy group's polarity may also disrupt hydrophobic P1 binding, though spectral interference precludes reliable activity assessment.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 18
description: Compound 18 (3-methyl-4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) shows autofluorescence, confounding anisotropy measurements. The 3-methyl group likely provides insufficient hydrophobic bulk for P1 engagement, based on inactive analogs like compound 1.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 19
description: Compound 19 (2-hydroxy-4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) exhibits moderate stabilization (CC₅₀ = 19 µM, SF = 4.9). The phenolic OH group enables polar interactions, but its reduced cooperativity (vs. halogenated analogs) limits α-factor enhancement in ternary complex formation.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 22
description: Compound 22 (4-(2-phenyl-1H-imidazol-1-yl)-1-naphthaldehyde) shows autofluorescence (ex/em profiles). The naphthalene extension creates steric clash in the binding groove (PDB: 7BGW), preventing productive stabilization despite covalent tethering potential.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 23
description: Compound 23 (2-bromo-4-(2-(2-bromophenyl)-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) is highly potent (CC₅₀ = 24 µM, SF = 18.9). The ortho-bromophenyl group rigidifies the ligand, optimizing hydrophobic packing (PDB: 7BG3). Its α-factor of ~60 reflects strong cooperativity, though saturation occurs at higher concentrations than compound 28.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 25
description: Compound 25 (2-bromo-4-(2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) is inactive (CC₅₀ >500 µM). The para-hydroxyl group disrupts hydrophobic P2 binding and may introduce electrostatic repulsion, negating the benefits of bromine-mediated P1 engagement.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 26
description: Compound 26 (2-bromo-4-(2-(pyridin-3-yl)-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) shows weak activity (CC₅₀ = 92 µM, SF = 2.3). The pyridinyl nitrogen’s basicity likely creates desolvation penalties in the hydrophobic pocket, reducing binding affinity despite structural mimicry of phenyl.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 27
description: Compound 27 (2-bromo-4-(2-(5-bromo-2-fluorophenyl)-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) achieves submicromolar stabilization (apparent K<sub>D</sub> = 0.78 µM, SF = 56.6). The halogen-rich aromatic system enhances hydrophobic complementarity (PDB: 7BDY), with an α-factor of ~60 and early saturation kinetics.

name: Pin1/14-3-3 compound 28
description: Compound 28 (2-bromo-4-(2-(2,4-difluorophenyl)-1H-imidazol-1-yl)benzaldehyde) is the most potent molecular glue (apparent K<sub>D</sub> = 0.27 µM, SF = 96.8, α-factor = 270). The 2,4-difluorophenyl group locks Asn42 into a conformation enabling a direct H-bond with Pin1's Gln+3 (PDB: 7BFW). This unique water-mediated network drives >250-fold selective stabilization over other 14-3-3 complexes.

This benzothiophene-linked fragment exhibited partial electron density in crystallography (PDB: 8BYG), suggesting suboptimal linker design. It partially stabilized the 14-3-3σ/ERα complex but required optimization. The benzothiophene moiety adopted an intermediate conformation between isolated and co-soaked fragments, while the p-chlorophenyl ring diverged from Compound 1’s binding pose. Though inactive as a potent stabilizer, it validated fragment-linking feasibility for orthosteric PPI stabilization, guiding subsequent SAR efforts toward rigidified linkers.

As the first active phenylthiophene-linked stabilizer (EC₅₀ ~311 μM), this compound demonstrated conserved binding modes of original fragments in its crystal structure (PDB: 8BYF). The amidine group maintained a salt bridge with 14-3-3σ Glu14, while the chlorophenyl moiety occupied a hydrophobic pocket formed by Phe119, Pro167, and ERα Val595. Its moderate stabilization (observed via fluorescence anisotropy) and clear electron density established the fragment-linking strategy’s viability for developing noncovalent PPI enhancers.

Replacing the ether linker with an amine (Y-position) slightly weakened stabilization compared to Compound 6. Crystallography (PDB: 8BYY) confirmed binding mode retention, but reduced potency highlighted the ether oxygen’s role in hydrophobic anchoring. The chlorophenyl group’s burial between 14-3-3σ and ERα Val595 remained critical, as its removal abolished activity. This analogue informed SAR on linker polarity’s impact on occupancy in the composite pocket.

Removal of the p-chloro substituent from Compound 6’s phenyl ring (W-position) resulted in >500 μM EC₅₀ and poor electron density (PDB: 8BXI). The unsubstituted phenyl lost critical hydrophobic contacts with 14-3-3σ residues (Phe119, Ile168) and ERα Val595, underscoring the halogen’s role in stabilizing the ternary complex. This loss-of-function mutant emphasized the pocket’s sensitivity to halogen-dependent van der Waals interactions.

Combining the aniline linker (Y=N) with unsubstituted phenyl (W=H) abolished stabilization (EC₅₀ >500 μM). Crystallography (PDB: 8BXM) showed reduced electron density and poor anchoring, confirming that both the aniline nitrogen and p-chloro group are essential for high-affinity binding. This "double-negative" variant reinforced the synergistic role of polar linkers and hydrophobic substituents in PPI stabilization.

Bromine substitution at the phenyl para-position (W=Br) maintained activity (EC₅₀ ~395 μM) and binding mode (PDB: 8BX3), comparable to the chloro analogue (Compound 6). The conserved interaction with Lys122 (4 Å distance) validated halogen tolerance in this hydrophobic pocket. This indicated that bulkier halogens could be accommodated without perturbing the stabilizer’s orientation, supporting strategic halogen scanning for potency optimization.

The p-CF₃ group (W=CF₃) yielded EC₅₀ ~398 μM and a conserved crystal structure (PDB: 8BWJ). Like Compound 12, it engaged Lys122 but showed no additional polar interactions despite the trifluoromethyl group’s electrostatic potential. Its potency parity with halogens suggested that hydrophobicity, not halogen-specific effects, dominates binding in this subpocket, guiding further substitutions.

Meta-chloro addition on the phenyl ring (V=Cl) retained stabilization (EC₅₀ ~314 μM) with unaltered binding (PDB: 8BX4). The meta-substituent pointed toward solvent-exposed regions, avoiding steric clashes with 14-3-3σ Lys122 or ERα Val595. This demonstrated tolerance for modifications at this position, enabling future functionalization for solubility or pharmacokinetics without disrupting core stabilizing interactions.

A meta-fluoro substituent (V=F) showed EC₅₀ ~332 μM (PDB: 8BYO), analogous to Compound 14. The fluorine’s small size and low polarizability prevented unfavorable interactions while minimally altering electron density. This confirmed meta-position flexibility for introducing fluorinated probes or metabolic stability tags without compromising molecular glue function.

Replacing chlorine with an acetyl group (W=COCH₃) abolished activity (EC₅₀ >500 μM) due to poor electron density (PDB: 8BWZ). The carbonyl failed to engage Lys122, likely due to desolvation penalties in the hydrophobic pocket. This underscored the pocket’s preference for nonpolar moieties over H-bond acceptors, discouraging polar substitutions at this site.

A p-methoxy group (W=OCH₃) improved electron density (EC₅₀ ~305 μM; PDB: 8BX0). The methoxy oxygen approached Lys122 (3.3 Å), suggesting a potential weak H-bond. This contrasted with acetyl failure, indicating that ether oxygen retains hydrophobic character while enabling polar contacts, offering a path to balance potency and solubility.

Cyclobutyl replacement of gem-dimethyl groups (X-position) was tolerated (EC₅₀ ~284 μM; PDB: 8BYE). The aliphatic ring maintained hydrophobic contacts with 14-3-3σ Leu218/Ile219 and ERα Val595. High-occupancy crystallography confirmed that small alicyclic rings preserve the stabilizer’s pose, enabling exploration of strain effects or conformational constraints in future analogues.

A cyclopentyl group at the X-position showed activity (EC₅₀ ~176 μM; PDB: 8BYD). Its larger ring enhanced hydrophobic interactions without perturbing binding, as validated by clear electron density. This demonstrated that expanded aliphatic systems can improve van der Waals contacts in the "roof" of the 14-3-3 binding groove, boosting potency.

Cyclohexyl substitution (X-position) exhibited moderate stabilization (EC₅₀ ~172 μM; PDB: 8BYB). The flexible ring adapted to the pocket, with crystallography confirming interactions with Val595 and 14-3-3σ residues. Its performance validated six-membered rings as viable hydrophobic anchors, informing designs to exploit deeper regions of the interface.

Tetrahydropyran at X-position (EC₅₀ ~301 μM; PDB: 8BXS) introduced an H-bond acceptor. The oxygen participated in a water-mediated network with ERα Val595’s backbone, enhancing solubility and reducing aggregation. This demonstrated how heteroatom incorporation in aliphatic substituents can improve physicochemical properties while maintaining stabilization.

Piperidine introduction (X-position; EC₅₀ = 118 μM; PDB: 8C0K) created a hydrogen bond donor. The amine engaged a water network linking ERα’s C-terminus and 14-3-3σ, contributing to its 21-fold complex stabilization. This marked the first significant potency jump, showing that polar interactions with both proteins enhance molecular glue efficacy.

4-Aminocyclohexyl substitution (X-position; EC₅₀ = 151 μM; PDB: 8BWX) delivered high selectivity for ERα over other 14-3-3 clients. The amine formed water-mediated H-bonds with ERα’s terminal carboxyl and 14-3-3σ, driving 25-fold stabilization – the highest in the series.
