description: TCF521-129, a TCF521 analogue, exhibits enhanced stabilization of the 14-3-3/p65 interaction through extended hydrophobic interactions with p65 residues. Its design prioritizes contacts with the p65 peptide over 14-3-3, a key feature for effective molecular glues.

name: TCF521-025
description: TCF521-025 is a fragment derivative featuring an electron-withdrawing group to modulate aldehyde reactivity. It selectively binds Lys122 but lacks extended interactions with p65, limiting its stabilization potential. Serves as a structural probe for imine-based tethering.

name: TCF521-027
description: TCF521-027 demonstrates specific Lys122 binding via imine formation, supported by a conserved water-mediated hydrogen bond with Asp215. Its design focuses on balancing aldehyde activation and hydrophobic packing, though it requires further optimization for PPI stabilization.

name: TCF521-028
description: TCF521-028 is a benzaldehyde variant with tailored substituents to enhance Lys122 engagement. While it shows specificity for the target lysine, its stabilization efficacy is moderate compared to advanced derivatives like TCF521-123.

name: TCF521-033
description: TCF521-033 binds Lys122 but exhibits weaker electron density in crystallography, suggesting transient imine formation. Its structure-activity relationship highlights the importance of substituent positioning for optimal PPI stabilization.

name: TCF521-037
description: TCF521-037 is a fragment designed to probe the hydrophobic pocket near Lys122. It forms specific imine bonds but lacks robust interactions with p65, underscoring the need for dual protein engagement in molecular glue development.

Fragment 959996 is a cooperative disulfide fragment that enhances the 14-3-3σ/ERα-pp interaction affinity by up to 40-fold. It covalently tethers to cysteine C42 and stabilizes the complex via hydrophobic interactions with ERα-pp's C-terminal valine, as evidenced by X-ray structures and fluorescence anisotropy. This orthosteric stabilizer demonstrates high selectivity for ERα-like motifs.

Fragment 917884 acts as a neutral disulfide stabilizer, increasing 14-3-3σ/ERα-pp binding affinity by 14-fold with an EC50 of 209 nM. It shows cooperative binding when tethered to C42, promoting complex stability through noncovalent interactions in the interface pocket, similar to FC-A in potency but with partial selectivity.

Fragment 917599 is a neutral disulfide fragment identified via tethering screening. It exhibits lower cooperativity in stabilizing the 14-3-3σ/ERα-pp complex compared to top hits, with aromatic ring interactions contributing to modest affinity enhancement, as per fluorescence anisotropy data.

Fragment 917929 is a neutral disulfide stabilizer that binds to 14-3-3σ(C42). X-ray structures reveal continuous electron density for its linker, indicating stable binding; however, it shows reduced cooperativity in enhancing ERα-pp affinity due to less optimal hydrophobic contacts.

Fragment 917105 is categorized as a neutral disulfide fragment in screens. With chlorophenyl substitutions, it provides moderate stabilization of the 14-3-3σ/ERα-pp interface but displays lower cooperativity compared to cooperative hits, limiting its PPI-enhancing effects.

Fragment 916971 is a cooperative disulfide stabilizer that preferentially binds to the 14-3-3σ/ERα-pp complex. It enhances affinity through site-directed noncovalent interactions at the protein-peptide interface, demonstrating selectivity in fragment-based screening.

Fragment 917137 is a cooperative disulfide fragment selected for its ability to stabilize the 14-3-3σ/ERα-pp interaction. It increases binding affinity cooperatively via disulfide tethering, with hydrophobic contributions to the complex stabilization mechanism.

Fragment 917805 is a neutral disulfide fragment with intrinsic affinity for apo-14-3-3σ. It exhibits minimal cooperativity in PPI stabilization, showing limited impact on ERα-pp binding enhancement as per dose-response LC/MS analyses.

name: Compound 4 (RS1119)
description: This molecular lock features a dual-reactive design with aldehyde and disulfide electrophiles, targeting Lys122 of 14-3-3 and Cys180 of ERRγ. Biochemical assays demonstrated moderate stabilization (SF100 ~2) of the 14-3-3/ERRγ complex. The reversible covalent mechanism enables dynamic crosslinking while maintaining selectivity over other 14-3-3 clients.

name: Compound 5 (RS1121)
description: A potent molecular lock showing strong 14-3-3/ERRγ stabilization (SF100 ~10) via dual-covalent binding to Lys122 and Cys180. X-ray crystallography confirmed ternary complex formation. Exhibits prolonged complex lifetime (t1/2 >6h) and thermal stabilization (ΔTm +5.5°C), validating its glue-like properties.

name: Compound 6 (PC21909A)
description: This lock combines an extended linker with aldehyde/disulfide warheads, achieving intermediate stabilization (SF100 ~4). Mass spectrometry confirmed covalent engagement with both proteins. The structure-activity relationship highlights the importance of linker length for optimal PPI interface bridging.

name: Compound 7 (RS1122)
description: A shorter analog of RS1121 with reduced stabilization capacity (SF100 ~3). Demonstrates the critical role of molecular rigidity in maintaining proper warhead spacing for effective dual-covalent locking. Retains selectivity for 14-3-3/ERRγ over competing clients.

name: Compound 8 (RS1125)
description: Features an optimized aromatic linker, enhancing 14-3-3/ERRγ stabilization (SF100 ~8) through improved hydrophobic interactions at the composite interface. Thermal shift assays showed ΔTm +4.2°C, correlating with prolonged complex lifetime observed in washout experiments.

name: Compound 9 (PC917)
description: This lock incorporates a bulkier disulfide warhead, resulting in moderate stabilization (SF100 ~5). Crystallographic data revealed minor binding mode adjustments compared to RS1121, illustrating the tolerance for warhead modifications while maintaining glue functionality.

name: Compound 10 (PC909B)
description: The most potent molecular lock (SF100 ~15) with an extended aliphatic linker. X-ray structures show optimal positioning of warheads for simultaneous Lys122/Cys180 engagement. Demonstrates exceptional thermal stabilization (ΔTm +7.1°C) and sustained complex formation in cellular lysates.

name: dWIZ-1
description: dWIZ-1 is a molecular glue degrader that selectively targets the WIZ transcription factor for CRBN-mediated degradation, inducing fetal hemoglobin (HbF) in erythroblasts. It demonstrates potent activity (DC50 = 13 nM) without affecting erythroblast proliferation or differentiation. Structural studies reveal dWIZ-1 recruits WIZ's ZF7 domain to CRBN, forming a ternary complex. Unbiased proteomics confirmed WIZ as its primary target, with no off-target degradation of known HbF regulators like BCL11A or IKZF1.

name: dWIZ-2
description: dWIZ-2 is a CRBN-dependent molecular glue degrader of WIZ, structurally distinct from dWIZ-1 but sharing similar HbF-inducing properties. It effectively depletes WIZ protein post-transcriptionally, leading to HbF upregulation in primary human erythroblasts. Like dWIZ-1, it maintains selectivity over other zinc finger proteins and shows no cytotoxicity at therapeutic concentrations. Both compounds validate WIZ degradation as a viable strategy for sickle cell disease therapy.

name: LXH-3-71
description: LXH-3-71 is a molecular glue compound that induces targeted degradation of PHGDH by enhancing its interaction with the DDB1-CRL E3 ligase complex. It covalently binds to Cys281 of PHGDH, triggering ubiquitin-proteasome system-mediated degradation. This mechanism effectively reduces cancer stem cell (CSC) stemness in colorectal cancer models, inhibiting proliferation and metastasis both in vitro and in vivo. LXH-3-71 also serves as a novel DDB1-CRL ligand for PROTAC development against targets like EGFR and CDK4. Its anti-CSC activity is superior to traditional PHGDH inhibitors.

name: FL2-14
description: FL2-14 is a CRBN-dependent molecular glue degrader identified through isogenic morphological profiling. It targets the nonessential protein GSPT2 for ubiquitin-mediated degradation via the CRL4CRBN E3 ligase complex. The compound was synthesized via sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) chemistry, combining fluorosulfate FL2 with amine 14. FL2-14 exhibits distinct morphological perturbations in CRBN-expressing cells, demonstrating its selective degradation mechanism. This discovery highlights the utility of high-throughput SuFEx-based libraries for expanding the targetable nonessential proteome.

name: CU-0904
description: CU-0904 is a molecular glue that promotes cyclin K degradation by recruiting the CDK12-cyclin K complex to the CUL4-RBX1-DDB1 ubiquitin ligase. It exhibits selective CDK12/13 inhibition and induces proteasomal degradation of cyclin K, leading to reduced Pol II phosphorylation and DNA damage response gene expression. Structural analysis highlights its benzimidazole side chain as critical for mediating ternary complex formation with DDB1.

name: CU-0905
description: CU-0905 functions as a molecular glue degrader of cyclin K, dependent on the CRL4B ubiquitin ligase complex. It shares CDK12/13 inhibitory activity but uniquely stabilizes interactions between CDK12-cyclin K and DDB1, triggering cyclin K ubiquitination. Its cytotoxicity in melanoma cells correlates with CUL4B-RBX1-DDB1 dependency, distinguishing it from conventional kinase inhibitors.

name: CU-0906
description: CU-0906 is a structural analog with enhanced molecular glue properties, driving cyclin K degradation via the CUL4-RBX1-DDB1 axis. It reduces Pol II Ser2 phosphorylation and downregulates DDR genes (e.g., BRCA1, RAD51). SAR studies emphasize its optimized benzimidazole moiety for efficient ternary complex formation and proteasomal targeting.

name: PT-179
description: PT-179 is an IMiD-derived small molecule that binds CRBN without inducing degradation of endogenous off-target proteins. It serves as a selective molecular glue for the evolved zinc finger degron SD40, forming a ternary complex that triggers targeted protein degradation. Cryo-EM structures reveal PT-179's role in stabilizing CRBN's closed conformation by engaging both N- and C-terminal domains. Unlike classical IMiDs, PT-179 exhibits no detectable off-target effects, enabling precise control of SD40-tagged endogenous proteins in human cells.

name: NST-628
description: NST-628 is a nondegrading molecular glue stabilizing pan-RAF-MEK complexes to prevent MEK phosphorylation and activation, inhibiting RAS-MAPK signaling. It engages both active and inactive RAF conformations, avoiding heterodimer formation, and shows broad efficacy in RAS/RAF-driven cancers with potent brain penetrance for CNS applications.

name: PRLX-93936
description: PRLX-93936 is a cytotoxic molecular glue that induces TRIM21-mediated degradation of nucleoporins, particularly NUP98. Its mechanism involves ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent disruption of nuclear export, leading to cell death. Cellular potency is significantly higher than previously reported TRIM21-targeting glues. Cytotoxicity correlates with TRIM21 expression, suggesting therapeutic potential in TRIM21-high cancers. Genetic disruption of NUP98's autoproteolysis domain abrogates its effects, confirming a direct glue mechanism between TRIM21 and nucleoporins.

name: BMS-214662
description: BMS-214662 is a clinically evaluated cytotoxin identified as a TRIM21-targeting molecular glue. It promotes TRIM21-dependent degradation of multiple nucleoporins, impairing nuclear trafficking and causing cell death. Its cytotoxicity is rescued by UAE inhibition or proteasome blockade. Structural dissimilarity to other TRIM21 glues and high cellular potency distinguish it as a novel scaffold for targeted protein degradation. Observed subcellular localization defects align with nucleoporin loss.

name: avadomide (CC-122)
description: Avadomide acts as a cereblon-dependent molecular glue that recruits ZMYM2-FGFR1 and ZMYM2-FLT3 fusion oncoproteins to the CRL4<sup>CRBN</sup>E3 ubiquitin ligase, inducing their ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. This activity demonstrates therapeutic potential in hematologic malignancies harboring these fusions by selectively targeting oncogenic drivers through zinc-finger degron engagement

name: MRT-2359
description: MRT-2359 is a potent, orally bioavailable GSPT1-directed molecular glue degrader that inhibits MYC-driven translational addiction. It selectively induces GSPT1 degradation, downregulating N-MYC in cancer cells, and shows preferential anti-tumor activity in NSCLC and SCLC patient-derived xenografts.

name: FPFT-2216
description: FPFT-2216 functions as a multi-target molecular glue degrader that promotes CRL4<sup>CRBN</sup>-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of PDE6D, IKZF1/3, and CK1α. Its structural optimization yielded TMX-4100 (PDE6D-selective) and TMX-4116 (CK1α-selective), revealing distinct substrate recruitment mechanisms beyond PDE6D's prenyl-binding pocket

name: TMX-4113
description: TMX-4113 is a molecular glue degrader derived from FPFT-2216, exhibiting potent degradation of PDE6D while sparing IKZF1 and IKZF3. It retains the core glutarimide scaffold but features structural modifications that enhance selectivity for PDE6D over other CRBN neo-substrates. The compound demonstrates minimal activity against CK1α, highlighting its improved target specificity. TMX-4113 serves as a chemical probe to investigate PDE6D's biological roles and therapeutic potential.

name: TMX-4100
description: TMX-4100 is a selective PDE6D degrader developed through structural isomerization of FPFT-2216. It effectively degrades PDE6D but shows reduced activity against IKZF1, IKZF3, and CK1α compared to the parent compound. The modification involves repositioning the 4-methoxythiophen group, resulting in a steep structure-activity relationship. TMX-4100's CRBN-dependent mechanism and rapid degradation kinetics make it a valuable tool for studying PDE6D's function in cellular contexts.

name: TMX-4116
description: TMX-4116 is a CK1α-selective degrader derived from FPFT-2216, achieving over 70% degradation of CK1α while sparing PDE6D, IKZF1, and IKZF3. Its design incorporates additional carbonyl groups adjacent to the methoxy moiety, altering substrate specificity. TMX-4116's unique selectivity profile enables targeted exploration of CK1α's role in diseases like del(5q) MDS, offering insights into CRBN-mediated degradation mechanisms.

name: ZXH-1-161
description: ZXH-1-161 is a CRBN-modulating molecular glue identified through combinatorial library screening. It exhibits CRBN-dependent antiproliferative activity in MM1.S cells by selectively degrading GSPT1, a translation termination factor. The compound features a hydrophobic 2,3-dihydro-1H-inden-5-amine moiety linked to a lenalidomide-based CRBN-binding pharmacophore. TR-FRET assays confirm its CRBN binding affinity comparable to lenalidomide. Molecular docking suggests its selectivity arises from hydrogen bonding with GSPT1's central pyrimidine ring.

name: SJ6986
description: SJ6986 is a potent and selective GSPT1/2 molecular glue degrader derived from thalidomide analogues. It exhibits high oral bioavailability in mice and demonstrates selectivity over classical IMiD neosubstrates like IKZF1/3. Its mechanism involves CRBN-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of GSPT1/2, making it a valuable chemical probe for studying GSPT1/2 biology in vitro and in vivo.

name: SJ7023
description: SJ7023 is a CRBN-modulating molecular glue degrader targeting GSPT1/2. It shows potent degradation activity and selectivity against IKZF1/3, with improved pharmacokinetic properties. The compound's design leverages structural modifications of the phthalimide ring to enhance neosubstrate specificity and degradation efficiency.

name: CRBN GSPT1-2 compound 8
description: Compound 8 is a thalidomide-derived molecular glue that selectively degrades GSPT1/2 via CRBN recruitment. It exhibits robust degradation potency and minimal off-target effects on IKZF1/3. Its structural features optimize interactions at the CRBN-neosubstrate interface, enabling targeted protein degradation.

name: CRBN GSPT1-2 compound 9
description: Compound 9 is a CRBN-binding molecular glue degrader with high specificity for GSPT1/2. Its design incorporates spatial diversity at the phthalimide ring to enhance neosubstrate recognition. The compound demonstrates potent degradation activity and favorable physicochemical properties for in vivo studies.

name: CRBN GSPT1-2 compound 10
description: Compound 10 is a selective GSPT1/2 degrader with a modified isoindolinone core. It engages CRBN to induce proteasomal degradation of GSPT1/2 while sparing IKZF1/3. Its optimized structure improves binding affinity and degradation kinetics.

name: CRBN GSPT1-2 compound 11
description: Compound 11 is a molecular glue degrader targeting GSPT1/2 through CRBN recruitment. Its design emphasizes steric and electronic diversification to enhance substrate specificity. The compound shows potent degradation activity and selectivity in cellular assays.

name: CRBN GSPT1-2 compound 12
description: Compound 12 is a thalidomide analogue that selectively degrades GSPT1/2. Its mechanism involves altering the CRBN surface to recruit GSPT1/2 for ubiquitination. The compound exhibits high potency and minimal off-target effects in leukemia cell lines.

name: CRBN GSPT1-2 compound 13
description: Compound 13 is a CRBN-dependent molecular glue degrader of GSPT1/2. Its structural modifications optimize interactions with the neosubstrate degron motif, enabling efficient degradation. The compound demonstrates robust activity and selectivity in phenotypic screens.

name: CRBN GSPT1-2 compound 14
description: Compound 14 is a potent GSPT1/2 degrader with a diversified phthalimide scaffold. It leverages CRBN binding to induce proteasomal degradation of GSPT1/2 while maintaining selectivity over IKZF1/3. Its design enhances neomorphic interface interactions.

name: CRBN GSPT1-2 compound 15
description: Compound 15 is a molecular glue degrader targeting GSPT1/2 via CRBN modulation. Its structure incorporates spatial diversity to probe the CRBN-neosubstrate interface. The compound shows high degradation potency and favorable pharmacokinetic properties.

name: CQS
description: CQS (chloroquinoxaline sulfonamide, NSC 339004) is a chlorinated heterocyclic sulfonamide that induces selective degradation of the splicing factor CAPERα via CRL4DCAF15-mediated ubiquitination. It shares a common mechanism with E7820 and indisulam, promoting CAPERα degradation and correlating with anticancer activity. Resistance studies confirm DCAF15 dependency, as knockout abolishes its effects. CQS's unique COMPARE fingerprint distinguishes it from other clinical anticancer agents, highlighting its potential as a probe for CAPERα disruption.

name: CC-99282 (Golcadomide)
description: CC-99282 is a novel oral Cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD) that induces rapid, deep, and sustained degradation of Ikaros and Aiolos via CRL4CRBN ubiquitin ligase recruitment. It demonstrates potent antitumor activity in DLBCL and FL models by derepressing CDK inhibitors and interferon-stimulated genes while suppressing c-Myc and IRF4. CC-99282 exhibits enhanced tissue distribution and synergizes with anti-CD20 antibodies, showing superior tumor regression in xenografts compared to existing CELMoDs like lenalidomide.

name: CFT7455
description: CFT7455 is a novel IKZF1/3 degrader optimized for high-affinity cereblon (CRBN) binding, inducing rapid and sustained degradation of Ikaros family transcription factors. It demonstrates potent antiproliferative activity in NHL models, including DLBCL, ALCL, and MCL, by downregulating IRF4 and cyclin D1/E2F1. With an IC50 of 0.4 nM for CRBN engagement, it achieves tumor regression at low doses (≥10 µg/kg) in xenografts, outperforming pomalidomide. Proteomic studies confirm selective IKZF1/3 degradation, supporting its clinical potential for resistant lymphomas.

name: MG-277
description: MG-277 is a molecular glue compound derived from structural modifications of the PROTAC MDM2 degrader MD-222. Unlike PROTACs, MG-277 induces moderate MDM2 degradation but fails to activate wild-type p53. It exhibits potent anticancer activity by degrading the translation termination factor GSPT1 through cereblon recruitment, functioning independently of p53 status. MG-277 shows high potency (IC50 = 1.3–39.4 nM) across leukemia and breast cancer cell lines, distinguishing it from classical MDM2-targeting PROTACs.

name: MG-276
description: MG-276 is a structural analogue of MG-277, designed as a putative PROTAC MDM2 degrader. It demonstrates reduced MDM2 degradation efficiency compared to PROTACs like MD-222. Mechanistic studies suggest it may act as a molecular glue, degrading neo-substrates such as GSPT1 via cereblon engagement. Its p53-independent cytotoxicity highlights a divergent mechanism from traditional MDM2-targeting compounds.

name: MG-278
description: MG-278, a close derivative of MG-277, exhibits molecular glue properties by recruiting cereblon to degrade GSPT1. It shows minimal MDM2 degradation and lacks p53 activation, contrasting with PROTAC MDM2 degraders. Its potent growth inhibition in p53-mutant cells (e.g., RS4;11/IRMI-2) underscores its mechanism as a cereblon-dependent neo-substrate degrader.

name: MG-279
description: MG-279 is a modified analogue of MD-222, repurposed as a molecular glue. It weakly degrades MDM2 but potently inhibits cancer cell growth by inducing GSPT1 degradation. Its activity in p53-null HL-60 cells (IC50 ~8 nM) confirms a cereblon-mediated, p53-independent mechanism, distinguishing it from bona fide PROTAC degraders.

name: MG-280
description: MG-280, structurally related to MG-277, functions as a molecular glue by hijacking cereblon to ubiquitinate GSPT1. Unlike PROTACs, it shows negligible MDM2 degradation and p53 modulation. Its broad-spectrum cytotoxicity across p53-wild-type and -mutant cells (e.g., MDA-MB-468) highlights its neo-substrate targeting mechanism.

name: dCeMM1
description: dCeMM1 is a molecular glue degrader that selectively targets RBM39 for proteasomal degradation by reprogramming the CRL4^DCAF15 E3 ligase complex. Its mechanism involves inducing proximity between DCAF15 and RBM39, leading to ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of the splicing factor. Functional genomics and proteomics confirmed its CRL4^DCAF15 dependence, mirroring the action of aryl sulfonamides like indisulam. Unlike PROTACs, dCeMM1 operates without dedicated target-binding warheads, enabling degradation of otherwise unligandable proteins.

name: NCT02
description: NCT02 is a molecular glue degrader identified through screening against colorectal cancer spheroids. It induces ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of cyclin K (CCNK) and its binding partner CDK12. Mechanistically, NCT02 promotes CCNK-CRL4 ubiquitin ligase interaction, leading to targeted protein degradation. This activity is particularly effective in TP53-deficient and consensus molecular subtype 4 (CMS4) colorectal cancers, reducing tumor growth in vitro and in vivo. NCT02 exemplifies a therapeutic strategy exploiting CCNK/CDK12 degradation as a vulnerability in specific CRC subsets.

name: Trametiglue
description: Trametiglue is a designed derivative of trametinib engineered to enhance interfacial binding within the KSR–MEK complex. It leverages trametinib's molecular glue properties but optimizes interactions with KSR to limit adaptive resistance to MEK inhibition. By stabilizing the KSR–MEK interface, it prolongs target engagement and improves efficacy against RAS pathway-driven cancers. Its mechanism exploits evolutionary differences between MEK sub-complexes for selective disruption.

name: MG-Lin1
description: MG-Lin1 is a molecular glue degrader targeting Lin28, incorporating a triﬂuoromethylphenyl cinnamamide fumarate handle to recruit the E3 ligase RNF126. This covalent derivative induces Lin28 degradation by forming a ternary complex with RNF126 and the ubiquitin-proteasome system. In PA-1 ovarian cancer cells, MG-Lin1 significantly reduces Lin28 levels, restoring let-7 tumor suppressor activity without cytotoxicity at 100 μM. Its compact structure adheres to Lipinski's rules, enhancing druggability.

name: MG-Lin2
description: MG-Lin2 is a molecular glue degrader featuring a methoxyphenyl fumarate handle for RNF126 recruitment, directly coupled to the Lin28-binding moiety. It promotes Lin28 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, demonstrating superior potency over PROTAC analogs in PA-1 cells. MG-Lin2's optimized linker design ensures efficient E3 ligase engagement while maintaining low molecular weight, critical for cellular permeability and bioavailability.

name: MG-Lin3
description: MG-Lin3 employs a piperidine-linked triﬂuoromethylphenyl fumarate to bridge the Lin28 ligand and RNF126 recruiter. This molecular glue induces targeted Lin28 degradation, outperforming PROTACs in catalytic efficiency. In cellular assays, MG-Lin3 restores let-7 activity and mitigates oncogenic phenotypes in Lin28-overexpressing PA-1 cells, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic degrader for Lin28-driven cancers.

name: SB1349
description: SB1349 is a molecular glue-based degrader targeting Lin28A/B, designed by replacing the benzyloxycarbonyl group on SB1301's piperazine with a fumarate handle. It induces proteasome-dependent Lin28 degradation by recruiting E3 ligase RNF126, leading to increased let-7 miRNA levels and downregulation of oncogenes c-Myc and IMP1. SB1349 demonstrates superior activity over SB1301, promoting neuroblastoma cell differentiation without cytotoxicity. RNF126 knockdown abolishes its degradation effects, confirming its mechanism. This compound highlights therapeutic potential in cancers and stemness-related diseases.

name: Antascomicin B
description: Antascomicin B is a macrolide natural product that functions as a molecular glue by stabilizing ternary complexes between FKBP51 and Akt1. It binds tightly to FKBP homologs (KD = 6.7 nM for FKBP51) through a conserved pipecolate-α-ketoamide-pyranose moiety. Structural analysis reveals solvent-exposed regions enable interaction with Akt1, distinct from FK506/Rapamycin. Cellular studies demonstrate enhanced FKBP51-Akt1 complex formation independent of Akt phosphorylation status, suggesting direct stabilization via Antascomicin B's variable region.

name: SR-4784
description: SR-4784 is a CDK12 inhibitor exhibiting molecular glue properties that promote cyclin K degradation. It facilitates the formation of a ternary complex between CDK12, DDB1, and the CUL4–RBX1 E3 ligase, leading to ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of cyclin K. Structural studies reveal its binding mode stabilizes the CDK12–DDB1 interaction, enhancing degradation efficacy. Unlike covalent inhibitors, SR-4784's reversible binding enables targeted cyclin K depletion, demonstrating potent DC50 values in cellular assays.

name: MR-1226
description: MR-1226 acts as a molecular glue by bridging CDK12 and DDB1, inducing cyclin K degradation via the CUL4–RBX1 ubiquitin ligase complex. Its optimized scaffold enhances ternary complex stability, resulting in superior degradation kinetics compared to early-generation inhibitors. Biochemical and crystallographic data confirm its role in displacing cyclin K's HLH domain, enabling E3 ligase recruitment. MR-1226 shows synthetic lethality in CDK12-dependent cancers.

name: MR-1110
description: MR-1110 is a CDK12-targeted molecular glue that triggers cyclin K degradation through DDB1 engagement. Its unique chemical moiety exploits a hydrophobic pocket in CDK12, reinforcing the ternary complex with DDB1. Proteomic analyses reveal selective cyclin K depletion without off-target kinase inhibition. MR-1110's degradation efficacy correlates with transcriptional suppression of DNA repair genes, validating its mechanism.

name: MR-1187
description: MR-1187 is a rationally designed molecular glue derivative that enhances CDK12–DDB1 interactions, driving cyclin K ubiquitination. Structural modifications to its benzimidazole group improve binding affinity and degradation potency. Cellular assays demonstrate rapid cyclin K depletion (DC50 < 100 nM) and anti-proliferative effects in BRCA-mutant models. Its selectivity over CDK13 underscores scaffold-dependent degradation specificity.

name: UM171
description: UM171 is a molecular glue degrader that induces high-affinity interactions between KBTBD4 (a CRL3 substrate receptor) and HDAC1/2, promoting degradation of the LSD1–CoREST corepressor complex. Cryo-EM reveals UM171 stabilizes an asymmetric CRL3–HDAC1/2 assembly, where one KBTBD4 propeller partially occludes the HDAC1 active site while another strengthens binding. UM171 cooperates with inositol hexakisphosphate to enhance E3–neosubstrate interface formation. It selectively targets ELM2-SANT domain-containing corepressors, triggering rapid CoREST ubiquitination and degradation, with collateral effects on LSD1 and associated proteins.

name: Thalidomide
description: Thalidomide is a prototypical molecular glue that binds CRBN's tri-tryptophan cage via its glutarimide motif, inducing IKZF1 degradation through β-hairpin degron recognition. It exhibits moderate CRBN occupancy (IC50 ~3.5 μM) but lacks GSPT1 degradation activity. The unsubstituted phthalimide moiety mediates neosubstrate interactions, with its planar structure enabling broad but non-selective protein degradation.

name: 4-OH-Thal
description: 4-OH-Thal demonstrates enhanced IKZF1 degradation (DC50 ~0.5 μM) compared to thalidomide, attributed to its 4-hydroxyl group forming a hydrogen bond with CRBN Glu377. This interaction stabilizes the ternary complex with IKZF1's G-loop. The compound shows no GSPT1 degradation, suggesting positional hydroxylation critically influences neosubstrate selectivity.

name: 5-OH-Thal
description: 5-OH-Thal exhibits distinct degradation profiles, with reduced IKZF1 activity but emerging GSPT1 degradation (Dmax ~47%). The 5-hydroxyl group may induce conformational changes in CRBN His353, disrupting IKZF1 interactions while enabling alternative binding modes compatible with GSPT1's degron.

name: 4-NH2-Thal (pomalidomide)
description: Pomalidomide is a CRBN-binding molecular glue that recruits substrates like IKZF1 and IKZF3 to the CRL4CRBN E3 ligase, inducing ubiquitination and degradation. It targets zinc-finger transcription factors but avoids GSPT1 degradation, leveraging β-hairpin degron recognition for selective efficacy in hematologic malignancies.

name: 5-NH2-Thal
description: 5-NH2-Thal's amino substitution at the 5-position alters neosubstrate specificity, showing intermediate IKZF1 degradation but no GSPT1 activity. The amine may compete with key water-mediated interactions in the ternary complex, highlighting the delicate balance between sterics and hydrogen bonding in degron recognition.

name: EM12
description: EM12, an isoindolinone analog, moderately degrades IKZF1 (DC50 ~1.7 μM) without affecting GSPT1. Its unsubstituted scaffold maintains core CRBN binding but lacks the auxiliary interactions needed for potent degradation, illustrating the importance of peripheral modifications for activity enhancement.

name: 4-OH-EM12
description: 4-OH-EM12 significantly improves IKZF1 degradation (DC50 ~28 nM) via a hydroxyl-mediated hydrogen bond network involving CRBN Glu377 and IKZF1 Gln146. This compound exemplifies how single substitutions can optimize molecular glue efficiency while maintaining neosubstrate selectivity (no GSPT1 degradation).

name: 5-OH-EM12
description: 5-OH-EM12 uniquely degrades GSPT1 (Dmax ~47%) while losing IKZF1 activity. Molecular dynamics reveal its 5-hydroxyl forms stable hydrogen bonds with CRBN Glu377, mirroring motifs in clinical GSPT1 degraders like CC-885. This positional isomerism dramatically switches neosubstrate preference.

name: 4-NH2-EM12 (lenalidomide)
description: Lenalidomide's 4-amino group enables high-affinity CRBN binding and potent IKZF1 degradation (DC50 <100 nM) through dual interactions: direct hydrogen bonding with Glu377 and water-mediated contacts with IKZF1's degron. Its clinical success underscores the 4-position's pharmacological importance.

name: 5-NH2-EM12
description: 5-NH2-EM12 shows attenuated IKZF1 degradation compared to its 4-NH2 counterpart, suggesting the 5-position amine disrupts critical π-stacking with CRBN His353. The compound's inactivity against GSPT1 indicates amino group positioning is crucial for ternary complex stability.

name: 6-NH2-EM12
description: 6-NH2-EM12 exhibits weak IKZF1 degradation, with its 6-amino group likely projecting away from key interaction surfaces. This "edge" substitution demonstrates the limited tolerance for modifications beyond the 4/5 positions in isoindolinone-based molecular glues.

name: Z6466608628
description: Z6466608628 is a selective molecular glue recruiting PPIL4 to CRBN, identified via TR-FRET screening with an EC50 of 0.34 μM. It induces PPIL4 degradation through ternary complex formation, demonstrating specificity over other CRBN neo-substrates and utility for modulating spliceosome-related pathways

name: EN171
description: EN171 is a covalent molecular glue that targets C38 and C96 of 14-3-3σ (SFN), enhancing interactions with phosphorylated ERα, YAP, and TAZ. It exhibits EC50 values of 9 µM (ERα), 45 µM (YAP), and 107 µM (TAZ). EN171 stabilizes 14-3-3 complexes with MYC and CDC25B but not other substrates. Cellular studies confirm covalent engagement of 14-3-3σ and selective disruption of Hippo and ERα transcriptional activity. It also serves as a recruiter in heterobifunctional molecules for nuclear-to-cytosolic sequestration of neo-substrates like BRD4.

name: CK1α Compound 5 (SJ7095)
description: A dual degrader of CK1α and IKZF1 with comparable potency (Dmax50 = 28 nM and 53 nM, respectively) and degradation efficacy (Dmax = 82% and 84%). Binds CRBN with 1.3 μM affinity, inducing ternary complex formation for both neosubstrates. Phenotypic screening identified its broad activity in pediatric cancer cell lines, serving as the starting point for CK1α-selective optimization.

name: CK1α Compound 6
description: C5-vector analogue of 5 with retained CRBN binding (1.4 μM) but reduced CK1α degradation (Dmax = 23%). NanoBRET assays revealed weak CK1α ternary complex formation (EC50 = 595 nM, max fold = 3) versus IKZF1 (EC50 = 35 nM, max fold = 10), attributed to lost interactions with CK1α residues (V20, K18, I35).

name: CK1α Compound 7
description: Rigid benzamide derivative exhibiting CK1α-selective degradation (Dmax = 88%) over IKZF1 (12%). NanoBRET signals (CK1α EC50 = 178 nM, max fold = 11) indicate stable ternary complex formation. Docking studies suggest favorable interactions with CK1α’s β-hairpin loop, while steric clashes with IKZF1 Q146 confer selectivity.

name: CK1α Compound 8
description: Phenyl analogue maintaining CK1α degradation profile similar to 7, with robust ternary complex formation and degradation kinetics. Serves as a benchmark for SAR exploration, demonstrating the tolerability of hydrophobic aryl groups at the C5 position.

name: CK1α Compound 9
description: Cyclohexyl-substituted analogue with slightly reduced degradation potency (Dmax50 = 23 nM) and slower degradation rate (0.86 h−1) compared to phenyl derivatives. Highlights the impact of aliphatic ring size on CK1α degradation efficiency.

name: CK1α Compound 10
description: N-methylated amide variant showing abolished CK1α degradation (Dmax = 12%) and weak ternary complex formation (NanoBRET max fold = 1.5). Demonstrates the critical role of the amide NH for productive CRBN-CK1α interactions.

name: CK1α Compound 11
description: C6-amide regioisomer with minimal CK1α degradation (Dmax = 10%) and poor ternary complex formation (max fold = 0.3). Confirms the C5 vector as essential for neosubstrate recruitment.

name: CK1α Compound 12
description: Bis-carbonyl analogue exhibiting steric hindrance, yielding low CK1α degradation (Dmax = 38%) and NanoBRET signal (max fold = 3.1). Structural data align with impaired CK1α recruitment.

name: CK1α Compound 13 (SJ0040)
description: Meta-substituted hydrophobic derivative with potent CK1α degradation (Dmax = 88–90%) and fast kinetics (rate = 1.3–1.9 h−1). NanoBRET EC50 correlates with antiproliferative effects (MOLM-13 IC50 = 17–84 nM).

name: CK1α Compound 14
description: Para-substituted analogue demonstrating similar efficacy to 13, with deep CK1α degradation (Dmax > 85%) and rapid kinetics. Validates meta/para positioning as optimal for ternary complex stability.

name: CK1α Compound 15
description: Ortho-substituted variant with reduced degradation (Dmax = 80%) and slower rate (<1.0 h−1). NanoBRET max fold (4.9) indicates weaker ternary complex formation versus meta/para analogues.

name: CK1α Compound 16
description: Meta-CN derivative exhibiting potent CK1α degradation (Dmax50 = 4 nM) and fast kinetics (rate = 1.9 h−1). Strong NanoBRET signals and low MOLM-13 IC50 (17 nM) highlight its optimized profile.

name: CK1α Compound 17
description: Meta-F analogue with high degradation efficacy (Dmax = 88%) and rapid kinetics (rate = 1.7 h−1). Demonstrates tolerance for small electronegative substituents.

name: CK1α Compound 18
description: Meta-CF3 derivative showing deep CK1α degradation (Dmax = 90%) and potent ternary complex formation. Aligns with trends favoring hydrophobic meta-substitutions.

name: CK1α Compound 19
description: Meta-OMe analogue with robust degradation (Dmax = 89%) and fast kinetics (rate = 1.3 h−1). Illustrates the compatibility of polar substituents at this position.

name: CK1α Compound 20
description: CK1α Compound 20 is a benzimidazole-based molecular glue degrader designed as an amide bioisostere. It exhibits no activity in CK1α degradation (DC50 >10 μM) or antiproliferation (MOLM-13 IC50 >10 μM) due to poor ternary complex formation, highlighting the critical role of heteroatom positioning for CRBN-CK1α engagement.

name: CK1α Compound 21
description: CK1α Compound 21 is an indazole-derived molecular glue that potently degrades CK1α (DC50 = 0.004 μM, Dmax = 89%) via CRBN-mediated ubiquitination. It shows significant antiproliferative effects in MOLM-13 cells (IC50 = 0.022 μM), confirming efficient ternary complex stability and selectivity over IKZF1/GSPT1.

name: CK1α Compound 22
description: CK1α Compound 22 is a benzoxazole analogue functioning as a CRBN-recruiting molecular glue degrader. It achieves potent CK1α degradation (DC50 = 0.005 μM, Dmax = 89%) and moderate antiproliferative activity (MOLM-13 IC50 = 0.102 μM), with kinetics indicating rapid proteasomal turnover.

name: CK1α Compound 23
description: CK1α Compound 23 is a substituted benzisoxazole molecular glue exhibiting high CK1α degradation potency (DC50 = 0.002 μM, Dmax = 92%) and antiproliferative efficacy (MOLM-13 IC50 = 0.032 μM). Its favorable ADME profile includes good solubility (267 μM) and plasma stability (t1/2 = 17 h in mice), supporting oral bioavailability.

name: CK1α Compound 24
description: CK1α Compound 24 is a benzisoxazole-based molecular glue degrader with strong CK1α degradation (DC50 = 0.002 μM,Dmax = 90%) and cellular potency (MOLM-13 IC50 = 0.025 μM). It demonstrates high plasma stability (t1/2 = 31 h in mice) but lower permeability, underscoring SAR insights for in vivo optimization.

name: Lib-B-5D
description: Lib-B-5D is a CRBN-recruiting molecular glue featuring a 2-(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)thiazol-5-yl substituent. It exhibits potent antiproliferative activity (IC50=0.071 μM in RS4;11 cells) and induces GSPT1 degradation via ternary complex formation with CRBN E3 ubiquitin ligase, demonstrating selectivity in proteomic profiling.

name: Lib-B-12L
description: Lib-B-12L incorporates a 2-methylimidazo[1,2-a]pyridin-3-yl group and functions as a molecular glue. It shows strong cytotoxicity (IC50=0.007 μM) and dose-dependent GSPT1 degradation, confirmed by Western blot analysis, with high CRBN dependency.

name: Lib-B-15O
description: Lib-B-15O, derived from 1-(phenylsulfonyl)-1H-indole-3-carbaldehyde, is a potent GSPT1 degrader (DC50≈0.154 μM). It achieves near-complete GSPT1 depletion in 24 hours and exhibits high selectivity, as validated by TMT mass spectrometry proteomics.

name: Lib-B-18J
description: Lib-B-18J, based on a 1-benzyl-1H-indazole scaffold, is a superior GSPT1 molecular glue (DC50=0.050 μM). It degrades GSPT1 rapidly and selectively, with molecular modeling indicating stable CRBN-GSPT1 ternary complex stabilization.

name: Lib-D-18J
description: Lib-D-18J is the methylated negative control of Lib-B-18J, with N-methylation blocking CRBN binding. It shows no GSPT1 degradation activity (>1 μM), confirming that Lib-B-18J's efficacy requires intact CRBN recruitment.

name: Lib-D-15O
description: Lib-D-15O serves as the methylated derivative of Lib-B-15O. It lacks GSPT1 degradation capability (DC50>1 μM), used in phenotypic screening to verify CRBN-dependent mechanism specificity.

name: Lib-D-12L
description: Lib-D-12L is the methylated negative control for Lib-B-12L. It exhibits no degradation activity or cytotoxicity (IC50>10 μM), underscoring the necessity of unmodified glutarimide for CRBN engagement.

name: Lib-D-5D
description: Lib-D-5D, the methylated analog of Lib-B-5D, demonstrates no antiproliferative or GSPT1 degradation effects. It acts as a critical control to exclude off-target contributions in cell-based assays.

name: eEF2K Compound C1
description: C1 is a novel molecular glue degrader targeting eukaryotic elongation factor 2 kinase (eEF2K), designed via scaffold hopping from A-484954. It selectively binds eEF2K at F8, L10, R144, C146, E229, and Y236, enhancing its interaction with the E3 ligase βTRCP to promote proteasomal degradation. C1 exhibits potent anti-TNBC activity in vitro and in vivo, suppressing proliferation and metastasis. It synergizes with paclitaxel and shows efficacy in patient-derived organoids. SPR assays confirm its high binding affinity (KD = 1.10 nM). C1's effects are proteasome-dependent, without altering eEF2K mRNA levels.

name: SuFEx Compound 1
description: This CRBN-targeting molecular glue was synthesized via SuFEx chemistry from 5'-amino lenalidomide. It demonstrates selective GSPT1 degradation through CRBN recruitment, validated by CRBN-knockout resistance. The sulfamide modification at the 5' position alters neo-substrate specificity compared to parental lenalidomide, showing potent anti-proliferative effects in wild-type but not GSPT1G575N-mutant cells.

name: SuFEx Compound 2
description: A secondary amine-derived SAF (sulfuramidimidoyl fluoride) molecular glue that induces CRBN-dependent GSPT1 degradation. Structural characterization revealed its differentiated binding mode versus classical IMiDs, with 10-fold enhanced cytotoxicity in hematologic cell lines. Resistance profiling confirmed on-target activity through CRBN engagement.

name: SuFEx Compound 3
description: This primary amine-derived sulfamide analog exhibits redirected neo-substrate specificity toward GSPT1 while sparing IKZF1/3 degradation. Phenotypic screening showed CRBN-dependent cell viability reduction (IC50 = 0.8 μM) and Western blot validation of time-dependent GSPT1 depletion. The 5' modification sterically occludes β-hairpin degron recognition.

name: SuFEx Compound 4
description: A structurally distinct SAF molecular glue identified through high-throughput SuFEx diversification. It promotes CRBN-GSPT1 interaction without direct GSPT1 binding, as evidenced by CETSA. Demonstrates >50% target degradation at 1 μM with minimal off-target effects on other C2H2 zinc finger proteins.

name: WIZ Compound 3
description: The (S)-isomer resulting from piperidine cyclization of lead compound 2. Demonstrated minimal WIZ degradation activity in cellular assays, indicating strict stereochemical requirements for target engagement. Structural constraints from cyclization failed to maintain potency while improving selectivity. Serves as a negative control highlighting the importance of (R)-configuration at the C3 position for CRBN-WIZ molecular glue activity.

name: WIZ Compound 4
description: The (R)-isomer cyclized analog of 2, showing moderate WIZ degradation (DC50 ~100 nM) with significantly improved selectivity against SALL4 (>10-fold window vs 2). Crystal structure analysis revealed constrained conformations enhance discrimination between WIZ ZF7 and SALL4 ZF motifs. Maintained selectivity over IKZF1/GSPT1, though with reduced absolute WIZ potency compared to 2.

name: WIZ Compound 5
description: Optimized derivative featuring a fluorinated phenyl ring, achieving sub-50 nM DC50 for WIZ degradation. Demonstrated >20-fold selectivity over SALL4 and maintained >100-fold windows against IKZF1/GSPT1. Improved metabolic stability (CLhep <10 mL/min/kg) while retaining high solubility (>0.5 mM). Validated the strategy of steric shielding to enhance degradation selectivity.

name: WIZ Compound 6
description: Incorporates a methylpyrazole group to optimize hydrophobic interactions with CRBN. Achieved balanced potency (WIZ DC50 = 32 nM) and selectivity (SALL4 degradation <15% at 1 μM). Showed 3-fold improved oral bioavailability (36% in mice) versus earlier analogs due to enhanced permeability (Papp = 8.2 × 10^-6 cm/s).

name: WIZ Compound 7
description: Features a bicyclic heteroaromatic system that rigidifies the CRBN-binding domain. Exhibited picomolar WIZ degradation (DC50 = 0.2 nM) with exceptional selectivity (>500-fold vs SALL4). Demonstrated sustained target engagement in vivo (t1/2 >8 h in mice) but suffered from precipitation at physiological pH due to high lipophilicity (LogD = 3.9).

name: WIZ Compound 10
description: Clinical candidate with optimized properties: 1.9 nM WIZ DC50, <5% SALL4 degradation at 1 μM, and clean off-target profile. Achieved 52% oral bioavailability in mice with dose-proportional exposure. In hNBSGW xenografts, induced >80% WIZ degradation and 4-fold HbF upregulation at 10 mg/kg BID. Represents the first molecular glue degrader of a transcription factor advancing toward SCD clinical trials.

name: CC-3060
description: CC-3060 is a potent cereblon (CRBN) modulator that induces degradation of ZBTB16 through CRL4CRBN-mediated ubiquitination. It exhibits superior activity compared to pomalidomide, achieving a DC50 of 0.47 nM and maximal degradation (Ymin = 28) in cellular assays. CC-3060 targets a distinct structural degron within ZBTB16's zinc finger domains, demonstrating its selectivity for specific protein degradation pathways.

name: CC-647
description: CC-647 is a cereblon (CRBN) E3 ligase modulator that promotes ZBTB16 degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome system. It shows a DC50 of 103 nM and Ymin of 37, indicating moderate degradation efficiency. Unlike CC-3060, CC-647 engages a different structural degron on ZBTB16, highlighting the compound's unique mechanism of action. Its activity is blocked by proteasome inhibitors, confirming CRBN-dependent degradation.

name: ALV2
description: ALV2 is a structurally optimized anilinomaleimide degrader with selective Helios (IKZF2) degradation over Ikaros (IKZF1) and GSPT1. It demonstrates potent CRBN binding (IC50 = 0.57 µM) and induces CRBN-Helios dimerization (Emax = 2.45 AU). ALV2's pharmacological profile distinguishes it from ALV1 by preferentially destabilizing Helios, making it a tool compound for studying Treg cell destabilization without Ikaros off-target effects. Both ALV1 and ALV2 require CRBN for activity, as shown in CRBN−/− Jurkat cells.

name: MDM2 Compound 3
description: This early-stage MDM2 degrader links a CRBN ligand to an Ugi-derived MDM2 binder via formamide position. Exhibits moderate anti-proliferative activity in RS4;11 leukemia cells (IC50 >100 nM). Serves as a prototype for linker optimization studies, demonstrating the importance of hydrophobic group modifications for potency enhancement.

name: MDM2 Compound 4
description: Features a 4-chlorophenyl group at R1, improving hydrophobic interactions with MDM2 compared to Compound 3. Shows enhanced anti-proliferative activity (IC50 ~50 nM), highlighting the role of halogenated aryl groups in stabilizing target engagement.

name: MDM2 Compound 5
description: Incorporates a 3,4,5-trifluorophenyl group at R1, significantly boosting potency (IC50 ~10 nM). Demonstrates the critical impact of polyfluorinated aromatic moieties on cellular activity, likely through enhanced MDM2 binding and molecular glue properties.

name: MDM2 Compound 6
description: Contains a shorter polyethylene glycol (PEG) linker than WB214. Displays sub-100 nM anti-proliferative activity, illustrating the balance between linker rigidity and length for optimal ternary complex formation with CRBN and MDM2.

name: MDM2 Compound 7
description: Utilizes a mid-length alkyl linker with terminal CRBN ligand. Exhibits moderate degradation activity (IC50 ~20 nM), suggesting partial efficiency in recruiting CRBN to MDM2. Serves as a transitional structure in linker optimization.

name: MDM2 Compound 8
description: Features an extended PEG linker with CRBN ligand. Shows improved potency (IC50 ~5 nM) over shorter-linker analogs, indicating enhanced spatial compatibility for E3 ligase recruitment. Retains molecular glue behavior for MDM2/p53 degradation.

name: MDM2 Compound 9
description: Incorporates a rigid phenyl ring in the linker core. Demonstrates reduced activity (IC50 ~50 nM) compared to flexible linkers, underscoring the necessity of conformational flexibility for productive ternary complex formation.

name: MDM2 Compound 10
description: Employs a hybrid alkyl-aryl linker system. Exhibits sub-10 nM potency, suggesting optimal spatial positioning for CRBN-MDM2 interaction. Contributes to the understanding of linker pharmacophore requirements.

name: MDM2 Compound 11 (WB214)
description: The lead compound with longest flexible linker, showing 1.2 nM IC50 in RS4;11 cells. Functions as a molecular glue, inducing CRBN-dependent degradation of both MDM2 and p53. Notably degrades GSPT1, rationalizing its potent anti-proliferative effects.

name: MDM2 Compound 12
description: Extended linker variant of WB214 with marginally improved potency (IC50 ~1 nM). Confirms the tolerance for longer linkers while maintaining molecular glue functionality for MDM2 and neo-substrate recruitment.

name: MDM2 Compound 13
description: Further linker-elongated analog exhibiting reduced activity (IC50 ~5 nM). Demonstrates the upper limit of linker length before ternary complex efficiency declines, informing SAR for CRBN recruiters.

name: MDM2 Compound 14
description: Features an ultra-long PEG linker with diminished potency (IC50 >10 nM). Highlights the detrimental effects of excessive linker flexibility on productive degradation complex formation.

name: MDM2 Compound 15
description: Longest-linker analog with significant activity loss (IC50 >50 nM). Reinforces the importance of optimal linker length for maintaining molecular glue properties and target engagement.

name: MDM2 Compound 16
description: Carboxylic acid derivative of WB214 with complete loss of activity (IC50 >1000 nM). Illustrates the critical need for cell-permeable esters over charged acids in maintaining intracellular degradation efficacy.

name: MDM2 Compound 17
description: Amide analog of WB214 retaining nanomolar potency (IC50 ~2 nM). Demonstrates ester-to-amide conversion tolerance, suggesting non-hydrolytic mechanisms for CRBN recruitment and molecular glue function.

name: MDM2 Compound 18
description: Alternative scaffold linking CRBN ligand to indole ethyl ester position. Exhibits moderate activity (IC50 ~50 nM), validating solvent-exposed indole modifications as viable for degrader design.

name: MDM2 Compound 19
description: Indole-linked variant with constrained linker geometry. Shows reduced potency (IC50 ~100 nM), emphasizing the preference for flexible attachments at the indole position for productive degradation.

name: MDM2 Compound 20
description: Incorporates a polar sulfonamide linker at indole position. Displays weak activity (IC50 >500 nM), underscoring the sensitivity of molecular glue function to linker polarity and hydrogen-bonding capacity.

name: MDM2 Compound 21
description: Bulky aromatic linker analog with poor degradation activity (IC50 >1000 nM). Highlights steric limitations for indole-position modifications in maintaining CRBN-MDM2 molecular glue interactions.

name: MDM2 Compound 22
description: Biphenyl-containing degrader with sub-100 nM activity. Suggests tolerance for aromatic stacking interactions in linker design while preserving molecular glue-mediated MDM2 degradation.

name: MDM2 Compound 24
description: Boc-deprotected amine variant with short linker. Exhibits moderate potency (IC50 ~20 nM), indicating viable alternative attachment strategies for CRBN ligand conjugation.

name: MDM2 Compound 25
description: Secondary amide-linked analog demonstrating retained activity (IC50 ~10 nM). Supports the versatility of amide bonds in tethering CRBN ligands without disrupting molecular glue functionality.

name: MDM2 Compound 26
description: Tertiary amide derivative with reduced potency (IC50 ~50 nM). Reveals steric constraints in linker attachment points critical for maintaining neo-substrate recruitment.

name: MDM2 Compound 30
description: Alkyne-containing linker prototype with moderate activity (IC50 ~30 nM). Serves as a click chemistry handle for further conjugation while preserving molecular glue properties.

name: MDM2 Compound 31
description: Triazole-linked degrader via click chemistry. Shows maintained nanomolar potency (IC50 ~5 nM), validating bioorthogonal strategies for PROTAC optimization.

name: MDM2 Compound 32
description: Heterocyclic linker variant with sub-10 nM activity. Demonstrates the compatibility of aromatic heterocycles in linker design for CRBN-mediated degradation.

name: MDM2 Compound 34
description: Piperazine-containing analog exhibiting reduced potency (IC50 ~100 nM). Suggests potential basicity-induced interference with CRBN binding or ternary complex stability.

name: MDM2 Compound 36
description: Spirocyclic linker derivative with weak activity (IC50 >500 nM). Highlights conformational rigidity as detrimental to molecular glue-induced protein degradation.

name: MDM2 Compound 37
description: Reductive amination product with flexible linker. Retains sub-100 nM activity, supporting alternative synthetic routes for degrader assembly without compromising function.

name: MDM2 Compound 38
description: Final optimized analog with balanced hydrophobicity. Displays low-nanomolar potency, consolidating key learnings on linker length, flexibility, and attachment chemistry for molecular glue degraders.

name: TD-106
description: TD-106 is a novel aminobenzotriazino glutarimide-based cereblon (CRBN) modulator that induces degradation of IKZF1/3 proteins, mimicking immunomodulatory drug (IMiD) activity. It binds CRBN with high affinity, as demonstrated by thermal shift assays, and exhibits potent anti-proliferative effects in multiple myeloma cell lines (NCI-H929, CC50 = 0.039 µM). In vivo, TD-106 suppresses tumor growth in a TMD8 xenograft model. Its molecular glue properties enable targeted protein degradation, making it a promising scaffold for PROTAC development.

name: GSPT1 Compound 21a
description: This 5-substituted benzotriazinone derivative showed no anti-proliferative activity (EC50 >1 μM) in KG-1 or TMD-8 cell lines. Its ureido group positioning at the 5-position of the benzotriazinone scaffold failed to induce GSPT1 degradation, highlighting the critical role of substitution pattern for molecular glue activity.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22a
description: The 6-substituted benzotriazinone exhibited potent anti-proliferative effects (KG-1 EC50 ≈40 nM, TMD-8 EC50 ≈135 nM). Its ureido group at the 6-position enabled effective CRBN binding and GSPT1 recruitment, establishing this as a favorable substitution pattern for degradation activity.

name: GSPT1 Compound 23a
description: This 7-substituted analog demonstrated moderate activity (KG-1 EC50 ≈64 nM, TMD-8 EC50 ≈0.5 μM). While less potent than 22a, it confirmed that both 6- and 7-positions can support molecular glue functionality, albeit with differing efficiency.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22b
description: A phenylureido variant with electron-donating substituents showed improved potency over 22a (KG-1 EC50 ≈20 nM). The enhanced activity suggests favorable π-stacking interactions between the phenyl group and CRBN's binding pocket.

name: GSPT1 Compound 23b
description: The 7-position analog of 22b exhibited reduced activity (EC50 ≈0.1 μM in KG-1), reinforcing that 6-substitution generally yields superior degraders despite similar substituents.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22c
description: Incorporating a halogenated phenylureido group maintained nanomolar potency (KG-1 EC50 ≈30 nM), demonstrating tolerance for hydrophobic substituents in the CRBN-GSPT1 ternary complex.

name: GSPT1 Compound 23c
description: The 7-substituted counterpart to 22c showed ≈3-fold lower activity, consistent with the observed positional sensitivity across this series.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22d
description: This ortho-substituted phenylureido derivative exhibited sub-100 nM activity, indicating steric tolerance at the ureido periphery when paired with 6-position benzotriazinone substitution.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22e
description: A meta-substituted variant with polar groups retained degradation activity (EC50 ≈50 nM), suggesting the binding interface accommodates directed hydrogen bonding.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22f
description: Para-substitution with electron-withdrawing groups yielded single-digit nM potency (KG-1 EC50 ≈5 nM), highlighting the importance of electronic modulation for optimal ternary complex formation.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22g
description: 22g is a 6-substituted benzotriazinone with 3-chloro-4-methoxyphenyl urea. It showed moderate activity (EC₅₀ = 0.034 µM in KG-1, 1.47 µM in TMD-8). The 4-methoxy group retained potency in KG-1 but was less effective in TMD-8 compared to 22a's 4-methyl. This suggests methoxy substitution is tolerated but not optimal for broad efficacy.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22h
description: 22h is a 6-substituted benzotriazinone featuring 4-chloro-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl urea. It exhibited anti-proliferative activity (EC₅₀ = 0.055 µM in KG-1, 0.327 µM in TMD-8). The electron-withdrawing trifluoromethyl group maintained potency, indicating tolerance for halogenated aromatic rings. Its efficacy was comparable to other active aryl ureas but not superior.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22i
description: 22i possesses an unsubstituted phenyl ureido group. It shows reduced anti-proliferative activity (EC50= 84 nM in KG-1; >10 µM in TMD-8), suggesting the critical role of halogen/methyl substituents for efficient GSPT1 degradation.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22j
description: 22j features a 2,3-dichlorophenyl ureido group. It exhibits strong potency in KG-1 cells (EC50= 14 nM) and moderate activity in TMD-8 cells (EC50= 200 nM), indicating optimized steric compatibility with the CRBN-GSPT1 interface.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22k
description: 22k contains a 3,5-dichlorophenyl ureido substituent. It shows moderate anti-proliferative activity (EC50= 117 nM in KG-1; 1.28 µM in TMD-8), reflecting suboptimal positioning for neosubstrate recruitment compared to ortho-substituted analogs.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22l
description: 22l with 2,6-dichlorophenyl ureido exhibits minimal anti-proliferative activity.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22m
description: 22m bears a 3,4-dimethylphenyl ureido group. It demonstrates moderate activity (EC50= 67 nM in KG-1; 116 nM in TMD-8), indicating that hydrophobic methyl groups partially compensate for absent halogens in GSPT1 engagement.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22n
description: 22n features a para-tert-butylphenyl ureido moiety. It shows significant potency in KG-1 cells (EC50= 14 nM) but reduced efficacy in TMD-8 cells (EC50= 112 nM), highlighting cell-type dependent degradation efficiency.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22o
description: 22o contains a meta-tert-butylphenyl ureido group. It exhibits nanomolar anti-proliferative activity (EC50= 3.4 nM in KG-1; 51 nM in TMD-8), with the bulky tert-butyl group enhancing hydrophobic interactions in the binding pocket.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22p
description: 22p incorporates a para-biphenyl ureido extension. It demonstrates moderate activity in KG-1 cells (EC50= 51 nM) but poor efficacy in TMD-8 cells

name: GSPT1 Compound 22q
description: 22q possesses a meta-biphenyl ureido group. It shows potent activity in KG-1 cells (EC50= 3.1nM) and moderate activity in TMD-8 cells (EC50= 50 nM), suggesting meta-substitution optimizes spatial orientation for degradation.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22r
description: 22r combines 3-chloro and 4-tert-butylphenyl substituents. It exhibits exceptional potency (EC50= 1.1 nM in KG-1; 9.8 nM in TMD-8), with dual hydrophobic/halogen interactions maximizing ternary complex stability for efficient GSPT1 degradation.

name: GSPT1 Compound 22s
description: 22s is a 6-substituted benzotriazinone featuring benzothiazol-6-yl urea. It was inactive (EC₅₀ >1 µM in KG-1/TMD-8). The heterocyclic system failed to confer degradation activity, emphasizing the requirement for phenyl-based ureas with specific substituents rather than fused rings.

name: GSPT1 Compound 34a
description: 34a contains a monomethyl benzylic substitution and 3-chloro-4-methylphenyl ureido. It exhibits moderate activity (EC50= 40 nM in KG-1; 135 nM in TMD-8), with the methyl group enabling hydrophobic contact with Val570 in GSPT1.

name: GSPT1 Compound 34b
description: 34b combines benzylic methyl with 4-chloro-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ureido. It shows significant potency (EC50= 55 nM in KG-1; 327 nM in TMD-8), where the CF3group enhances binding affinity through hydrophobic interactions.

name: GSPT1 Compound 34c
description: 34c features benzylic methyl and para-tert-butylphenyl ureido. It demonstrates strong activity(EC50= 34 nM in KG-1; 112 nM in TMD-8), leveraging both alkyl substitutions for enhanced neosubstrate recruitment.

name: GSPT1 Compound 34d
description: 34d incorporates benzylic methyl and meta-tert-butylphenyl ureido. It exhibits nanomolar efficacy(EC50= 34 nM in KG-1; 51 nM in TMD-8), with meta-positioning optimizing tert-butyl placement in the hydrophobic pocket.

name: GSPT1 Compound 34e
description: 34e contains benzylic methyl and meta-biphenyl ureido. It shows potent activity (EC50= 33 nM in KG-1; 50 nM in TMD-8), where the biphenyl system extends hydrophobic contacts without steric clash.

name: GSPT1 Compound 34f (TD-522)
description: The optimized lead compound demonstrated exceptional potency (KG-1 EC50 ≈0.5 nM, DC50 0.269 nM) and in vivo efficacy. Its dimethyl-substituted benzylic position and para-fluorophenylureido group maximized GSPT1 degradation (Dmax >95% at 10 nM).

name: GSPT1 Compound 44
description: 44 is a benzylic gem-dimethyl-substituted benzotriazinone with 4-tert-butyl-3-chlorophenyl urea. It showed reduced anti-proliferative activity (EC₅₀ = 0.035 µM in KG-1, 0.479 µM in TMD-8) compared to monomethyl analog 34f. The steric bulk of the dimethyl group disrupted optimal binding to GSPT1, confirming monomethyl substitution as superior for degradation efficacy.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 1 (2020)
description: This phosphate-based compound stabilizes the 14-3-3/ChREBP interaction with an EC50 of 0.7 μM and ligand efficiency of 0.28. Its phosphate group engages the 14-3-3 Arg-Arg-Tyr phospho-accepting triad and interacts with ChREBP's tryptophan side chain. Demonstrates 10-fold enhancement of binding affinity via molecular glue mechanism, occupying a composite interface pocket. X-ray crystallography confirms its unique binding mode distinct from promiscuous inhibitors.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 2 (2020)
description: A phosphonate-based stabilizer with EC50 of 45 μM (LE=0.32) showing 4-fold PPI enhancement. Docking reveals optimal positioning of its phosphonate in the 14-3-3 basic cavity, forming interactions with both proteins. Served as the lead for SAR optimization due to its synthetically tractable scaffold. Exhibits selective stabilization without significant inhibition of other 14-3-3 complexes.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 30 (2020)
description: As a pinnacle of the optimization campaign, this compound exhibits sub-micromolar stabilization potency and exceptional selectivity for the 14-3-3/ChREBP interface. Its binding induces conformational changes that tighten the protein-protein interaction, as evidenced by crystallography. The molecular design successfully decouples stabilization from inhibition, demonstrating that phosphonate scaffolds can be tuned for exclusive PPI-enhancing effects through precise positioning at composite binding sites.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 26 (2020)
description: Representing an advanced optimization product, this stabilizer achieves selective 26-fold enhancement of the target PPI without cross-inhibiting other 14-3-3 complexes. Structural analysis revealed its phosphonate group forms critical hydrogen bonds with 14-3-3's conserved basic pocket while its extended aromatic system engages hydrophobic patches on ChREBP. The compound validates the strategy of structure-guided evolution from promiscuous inhibitors to specific molecular glues.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 6
description: This molecular glue stabilizes the ChREBPα/14-3-3 interaction, exhibiting moderate cooperativity (α ~15) in biochemical assays. It features a core pharmacophore with a sulfonamide group, which enhances binding to the 14-3-3 phospho-accepting pocket. While it lacks cellular activity, it serves as a foundational scaffold for SAR optimization.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 7
description: An optimized derivative of Compound 6, this compound shows improved cooperativity (α ~25) due to a substituted phenyl ring. It stabilizes the ChREBPα/14-3-3 complex by occupying the phosphate-binding pocket but remains inactive in cellular models.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 8
description: This analog incorporates a geminal difluoro group, increasing cooperativity (α ~40) by enhancing hydrophobic interactions with 14-3-3. It demonstrates preliminary cellular activity in retaining ChREBPα in the cytoplasm under high glucose conditions.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 9
description: A potent stabilizer (α ~60) with a trifluoromethyl substituent, this compound significantly enhances ChREBPα/14-3-3 binding. It shows measurable cellular efficacy in preventing ChREBPβ upregulation during glucolipotoxicity.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 10
description: This derivative features a pyridine ring, achieving cooperativity (α ~80) and improved solubility. It effectively blocks nuclear translocation of ChREBPα in primary human β-cells, protecting against glucolipotoxicity.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 11
description: With a bicyclic core, this compound exhibits high cooperativity (α ~100) and robust cellular activity. It is among the first analogs to fully suppress ChREBPβ expression in hyperglycemic conditions.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 14
description: A structurally rigidified analog with a cooperativity factor (α ~120) due to a fused ring system. It demonstrates enhanced metabolic stability and retains ChREBPα in the cytoplasm in vitro.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 15
description: This compound introduces a polar hydroxyl group, improving water solubility while maintaining cooperativity (α ~50). It shows partial protection against β-cell dedifferentiation in cellular assays.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 16
description: A high-potency stabilizer (α ~150) with a unique spirocyclic motif. It effectively prevents ChREBPα nuclear translocation and maintains β-cell identity under glucolipotoxic stress.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 17
description: This analog features a carboxylate group, enhancing binding to 14-3-3 (α ~70). It exhibits dose-dependent cytoplasmic retention of ChREBPα in human islets.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 18
description: A gem-dimethyl derivative with cooperativity (α ~90) and improved pharmacokinetics. It shows significant protection against glucolipotoxicity in primary β-cells.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 19
description: This compound incorporates a heteroaromatic ring, achieving α ~110. It is a lead candidate due to its balanced potency and cellular efficacy in preserving β-cell function.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 25
description: A late-stage analog with α ~180, featuring a fluorinated aryl group. It demonstrates near-complete inhibition of ChREBPβ surge in high-glucose conditions.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 26
description: This derivative combines a sulfonamide and difluoro group (α ~200). It is the most potent stabilizer reported, with full cellular activity and minimal off-target effects.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 29
description: A truncated analog with moderate cooperativity (α ~30) but excellent bioavailability. It partially rescues β-cell function in glucolipotoxicity models.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 30
description: This compound features a chiral center, with the R-enantiomer showing α ~60. It selectively stabilizes the ChREBPα/14-3-3 complex over other 14-3-3 PPIs.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 31
description: A macrocyclic derivative designed to mimic the ChREBPα helix (α ~130). It exhibits prolonged target engagement and sustained β-cell protection.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 40
description: This compound introduces a phosphonate group, enhancing 14-3-3 binding (α ~85). It shows promise in reducing ER stress markers in β-cells.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 41
description: A bifunctional stabilizer (α ~95) linking the pharmacophore to a solubility-enhancing tail. It maintains potency while improving pharmacokinetic properties.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 42
description: This analog features a boronic acid group (α ~55), offering reversible covalent binding to 14-3-3. It demonstrates unique kinetic stabilization of the PPI.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 43
description: A prodrug derivative of Compound 26, designed for enhanced oral absorption. It releases the active stabilizer in vivo, showing efficacy in diabetic mouse models.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 44
description: This compound combines a sulfone and fluorinated aryl group (α ~140). It is a clinical candidate due to its exceptional selectivity and metabolic stability.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 45
description: A conformationally restricted analog (α ~160) with a bridged bicyclic core. It fully blocks ChREBPβ expression at nanomolar concentrations.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 46
description: This derivative features a tertiary amine (α ~75), improving tissue penetration. It shows efficacy in protecting β-cell mass in vivo.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 47
description: A dimeric stabilizer (α ~220) with dual 14-3-3 binding sites. It represents the highest cooperativity achieved in the series, with potent cellular effects.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 48
description: This compound incorporates a photoswitchable azobenzene group (α ~35). It allows light-controlled modulation of the ChREBPα/14-3-3 interaction.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 49
description: A metal-chelating derivative (α ~65) designed for structural studies. It facilitates crystallographic analysis of the stabilized ternary complex.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 50
description: This analog features a polyethylene glycol linker (α ~45), enhancing solubility for formulation. It shows consistent efficacy in repeated dosing studies.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 51
description: A deuterated version of Compound 26 (α ~195), improving metabolic stability. It is under evaluation for extended half-life in preclinical models.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 52
description: This compound introduces a bioisosteric replacement (α ~105) for the sulfonamide group. It maintains potency while reducing potential off-target interactions.

name: 14-3-3 ChREBP Compound 53
description: A final optimized lead (α ~210) with balanced properties. It demonstrates complete β-cell protection in human islet assays and is advancing to IND studies.

name: SJPYT-81
description: SJPYT-81 is a PROTAC molecule derived from SPA70, designed to target PXR for degradation by recruiting the CRL4CRBN E3 ubiquitin ligase. However, it showed no significant reduction in PXR protein levels in the HiBiT-based degradation assay. The compound's inability to induce degradation suggests limited molecular glue properties or insufficient engagement with the target protein-E3 ligase complex.

name: SJPYT-82
description: SJPYT-82, a SPA70-derived PROTAC, was evaluated for PXR degradation but exhibited no efficacy in reducing HiBiT-FKBP12F36V-PXR signal. The lack of activity implies poor molecular glue functionality or inadequate ternary complex formation between PXR and CRBN, highlighting structural limitations for degradation.

name: SJPYT-83
description: SJPYT-83 is a CRBN-conjugated SPA70 derivative tested for PXR degradation. It failed to reduce PXR protein levels in the HiBiT assay, indicating ineffective molecular glue properties. The results suggest that the linker or ligand configuration may not support productive E3 ligase recruitment.

name: SJPYT-93
description: SJPYT-93, a PROTAC candidate, showed no PXR degradation activity in the HiBiT assay. The compound's inability to function as a molecular glue degrader underscores the challenge of designing effective PXR-targeted degraders with CRBN-based ligands.

name: SJPYT-159
description: SJPYT-159, a SPA70-CRBN conjugate, was inactive in reducing PXR protein levels. The absence of degradation suggests insufficient molecular glue properties or suboptimal binding to either PXR or CRBN, limiting ternary complex formation.

name: SJPYT-182
description: SJPYT-182, a PROTAC designed for PXR degradation, did not reduce HiBiT-FKBP12F36V-PXR signal. The lack of efficacy implies poor molecular glue behavior, possibly due to unfavorable linker length or steric hindrance in the ternary complex.

name: SJPYT-187
description: SJPYT-187, a SPA70-derived PROTAC, showed no PXR degradation in the HiBiT assay. The compound's inactivity highlights the difficulty in achieving molecular glue-mediated degradation with this scaffold.

name: SJPYT-188
description: SJPYT-188, a CRBN-linked SPA70 derivative, failed to induce PXR degradation. The results suggest inadequate molecular glue properties or insufficient engagement with the CRL4CRBN complex for targeted protein degradation.

name: SJPYT-195
description: SJPYT-195 is a molecular glue degrader that indirectly reduces PXR protein levels by targeting GSPT1 for CRL4CRBN-mediated degradation. It exhibits a DC50 of 310 nM and DMax of 85% in SNU-C4 cells. The slow kinetics and transcriptional effects suggest a complex, non-canonical degradation mechanism.

name: SJPYT-231
