name: S656
description: S656 is a molecular glue degrader targeting IKZF2 and CK1α through CRBN recruitment. It features a naphthamide scaffold that enables dual degradation activity in MOLM-13 AML cells. The compound demonstrates improved selectivity for IKZF2 over IKZF1 compared to earlier analogs, with structural rigidity enhancing target specificity. Key findings show S656 induces differentiation and apoptosis in leukemia cells while maintaining favorable pharmacokinetic properties for in vivo studies.

name: UOM-005428
description: UOM-005428 is a CRBN-binding molecular glue derived from lenalidomide analogs. It incorporates an extended aromatic system to promote IKZF2 degradation via π-stacking interactions with IKZF2's β-hairpin motif. The compound shows moderate degradation of both IKZF2 and IKZF1 in MOLM-13 cells, with the naphthalene moiety critical for target engagement. Optimization focused on reducing IKZF1 degradation while maintaining IKZF2 activity.

name: UOM-005550
description: UOM-005550 features a methoxy-substituted naphthyl group attached to the isoindolinone core. This modification enhances IKZF2 degradation potency (relative ratio = 0.43) while maintaining some IKZF1 activity. The 6-methoxy group's position proves critical for degradation efficiency, as positional isomers lose activity. The compound represents an intermediate in the development of more selective dual degraders like DEG-35.

name: UOM-005606
description: UOM-005606 is a dibenzofuran-based CRBN ligand that demonstrates IKZF2 degradation capability. The oxygen-bridged biaryl system provides structural rigidity, with linkage position (4 vs 3) significantly affecting degradation profiles. While maintaining IKZF1 degradation, this compound showed reduced IKZF2 activity compared to naphthyl analogs, guiding scaffold optimization toward naphthamides.

name: UOM-005608
description: UOM-005608 is a quinoline-modified molecular glue designed to probe heteroaryl effects on IKZF2 selectivity. The nitrogen-containing aromatic system alters electron distribution compared to naphthyl analogs, resulting in attenuated IKZF2 degradation. This compound helped establish the superiority of purely hydrocarbon aromatic systems for maintaining IKZF2 degradation potency in the series.

name: UOM-005636
description: UOM-005636 represents a dimethoxy-naphthyl derivative that maintains dual IKZF1/IKZF2 degradation activity. Among methoxy-substituted analogs, this compound showed the most balanced degradation profile, though with less IKZF2 selectivity than desired. The compound informed subsequent design of constrained analogs through amide linkage (e.g., DEG-35) to improve selectivity.

name: Dec-60
description: 12-60 is a novel CRBN-recruiting molecular glue degrader that selectively targets GSPT1 for ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation. It exhibits potent CRBN-dependent antiproliferative activity in MDA-MB-231 cells (IC50 = 2.07 μM), with proteomic and transcriptomic analyses confirming on-target effects on translation regulation. Its mechanism involves ternary complex formation with CRBN and GSPT1, showing comparable efficacy to CC-90009.

name: KMG-1068
description: KMG-1068 is an isoindolinone glutarimide-based molecular glue degrader demonstrating selective IKZF2 degradation while sparing CK1α. It achieves potent IKZF2 degradation (DC50 < 10 nM) through CRBN-mediated ubiquitination, with minimal off-target effects on structurally related neosubstrates. Structural optimization focused on the azaindazole core to disrupt CK1α binding while maintaining IKZF2 engagement. Key interactions involve the conserved tryptophan pocket in CRBN's thalidomide-binding domain. This compound exemplifies successful selectivity tuning in molecular glue design.

name: AB138
description: AB138 is a novel molecular glue degrader that targets GSPT1 by recruiting it to the CRBN E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, inducing rapid and sustained degradation. It activates the integrated stress response, downregulates MCL1 and c-Myc oncoproteins, and triggers apoptosis in acute myeloid leukemia cells, demonstrating potent in vitro and in vivo anti-leukemic efficacy without overt toxicity.
A spiro-iso-indolinone-based molecular glue degrader with potent IKZF2 degradation (DC50= 9.7 nM, Dmax= 70%). It exhibits high selectivity over IKZF1/3, GSPT1, and CK1α, minimal SALL4 degradation.

A difluorinated piperidine analog demonstrating effective IKZF2 degradation (DC50= 5.7 nM, Dmax= 68%). Fluorination maintains degradation potency while potentially mitigating hERG liability. It retains the core spirocyclic scaffold critical for CRBN-mediated IKZF2 ubiquitination.

Achieves comparable IKZF2 degradation (DC50= 16 nM, D<sub>max</sub>= 69%) to Compound 5. The cyclohexylmethyl substitution replaces the benzyl group, preserving molecular glue function and selectivity against off-target neo-substrates (IKZF1/3, GSPT1, CK1α).

A pyridylmethyl derivative with moderate IKZF2 degradation activity (DC50= 18 nM, Dmax= 64%). The heteroaromatic tail slightly reduces potency compared to benzyl or thiophene analogs, highlighting the importance of tail hydrophobicity/electronics for ternary complex stability.

A thiophene-containing degrader with enhanced IKZF2 degradation (DC50= 5.9 nM, Dmax= 84%). The electron-rich thiophene tail improves efficacy over Compound 5, underscoring the role of aromatic interactions in optimizing CRBN-IKZF2 molecular gluing.

The lead compound featuring a meta-(1-methylpyrazole)benzyl tail. It achieves sub-nanomolar IKZF2 degradation (DC50= 0.8 nM, Dmax= 89%) with exceptional selectivity. Its S-enantiomer (PVTX-405) shows superior DC50(0.7 nM) and oral bioavailability, driving in vivo efficacy in tumor models.

name: PVTX-405(16a)
description: PVTX-405(16a) is a cyclin K MGD derived from compound 16, with further optimized DDB1-binding properties. It exhibits superior degradation efficiency and AML selectivity, attributed to its tailored hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions within the DDB1 pocket.

name: 16b
description: Compound 16b is a cyclin K degrader variant with structural tweaks to the terminal group, improving DDB1 binding kinetics. It maintains potent cyclin K degradation while reducing off-target CDK inhibition, as validated in AML cell models.

13-7 is a highly cooperative molecular glue inducer of protein-protein associations, binding BRD9 and the VCB complex with nanomolar ternary affinity (α > 159 for BRD9). It promotes stable ternary complex formation without a hook effect, as validated by AlphaScreen, SPR, and cellular NanoBiT assays. Its cooperativity enables selective degradation of BRD9 over homolog BRD7.

name: dGEM3
description: dGEM3 is a molecular glue degrader that selectively targets GSPT1 for proteasomal degradation by recruiting it to the E3 ubiquitin ligase CRBN. It exhibits potent anti-leukemic activity in AML models by inducing sustained GSPT1 depletion, leading to integrated stress response activation (eIF2α phosphorylation, ATF3/CHOP upregulation) and downregulation of oncoproteins MCL1 and c-Myc. This triggers caspase-3/PARP cleavage and apoptosis. Unlike CC-885, dGEM3 shows improved selectivity, reducing off-target toxicity while maintaining efficacy in xenograft models.

name: LHS no oxygen
description: LHS no oxygen is a structural analog of AB138 with a modified linker region lacking an oxygen atom. It retains GSPT1-degrading activity but exhibits reduced binding affinity to CRBN, resulting in slower degradation kinetics. Mechanistically, it still induces ISR activation and MCL1/c-Myc downregulation, though with attenuated potency compared to AB138. This variant highlights the importance of linker chemistry in molecular glue efficiency.

name: RHS no ortho chlorine
description: RHS no ortho chlorine is an AB138 derivative missing the ortho-chlorine substituent on its right-hand side. This modification weakens ternary complex formation with CRBN-GSPT1, impairing degradation efficiency. While it maintains residual activity in stress response induction, its anti-leukemic effects are diminished, underscoring the critical role of halogen interactions in stabilizing the degrader-target-ligase interface.

name: CPD1
description: CPD1 is an initial hit compound identified as a SUMO1 degrader, inducing ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of SUMO1 through the CAPRIN1-FBXO42-CUL1 E3 ligase pathway. It selectively reduces SUMO1 conjugation and inhibits cancer cell proliferation across multiple tumor types, serving as a foundation for lead optimization.

name: HB007
description: HB007 is an optimized lead molecular glue degrader derived from CPD1 that binds CAPRIN1, promoting SUMO1 recruitment to the CUL1 E3 ligase for ubiquitination and degradation. It exhibits selective anti-tumor activity, suppresses patient-derived xenograft progression in various cancers, and extends survival in murine models without significant off-target effects.

name: LYG-101
description: LYG-101 is a GSPT1-targeting molecular glue degrader featuring an oxime-modified difluoroacetamide group. It induced 82.63% GSPT1 degradation at 200 nM in KG-1 AML cells, outperforming CC-90009 (58.69%). The electron-withdrawing fluorine substituent at R₂ enhances ternary complex formation with CRBN and GSPT1. While demonstrating improved degradation efficacy over lead compounds, its metabolic stability limitations preclude further development.

name: LYG-102
description: This chloro-substituted molecular glue degrader contains a hydrogen-bond accepting oxime moiety. LYG-102 achieved 74.02% GSPT1 degradation at 200 nM in KG-1 cells via CRL4CRBN-mediated ubiquitination. Its antiproliferative activity remains unquantified, but structural analysis indicates the chlorine atom at R₂ potentially enhances target engagement through halogen bonding interactions within the GSPT1 binding pocket.

name: LYG-103
description: Featuring a bromine substituent, LYG-103 is a molecular glue that degraded 68.48% of GSPT1 at 200 nM. The bromine atom's increased steric bulk and polarizability relative to chloro/fluoro analogs may contribute to its distinct binding mode. Proteasome inhibition studies confirm its mechanism relies on ubiquitin-proteasome pathway activation.

name: LYG-105
description: LYG-105 incorporates a morpholine-substituted benzylidene group. It showed moderate GSPT1 degradation (34.38% at 200 nM), attributed to steric hindrance from the bulky morpholine moiety impeding optimal positioning in the β-sheet core of GSPT1 domain 3. This structural feature highlights the sensitivity of molecular glue efficacy to side-chain spatial constraints.

name: LYG-106
description: This methyl-chloro substituted oxime degrader demonstrates exceptional potency, degrading 88.86% of GSPT1 at 200 nM with KG-1 IC₅₀ = 3.75 ± 0.51 nM. The methyl group at R₂ and chlorine at R₃ synergistically enhance ternary complex stability. However, its metabolic half-life (T₁/₂ = 11.40 min in rat microsomes) limits therapeutic utility despite significant target engagement.

name: LYG-108
description: LYG-108 features a hydrazone-modified acetamide group, achieving 82.19% GSPT1 degradation at 200 nM and KG-1 IC₅₀ = 6.19 ± 1.17 nM. The hydrazone moiety serves as a hydrogen-bond acceptor, mimicking the oxime function in analogs like LYG-106 while offering distinct electronic properties that contribute to its degradation efficacy.

name: LYG-201
description: As a primary amine derivative, LYG-201 exhibited reduced degradation activity (34.73% at 200 nM). The unmodified amine fails to replicate the hydrogen-bond network established by oxime-containing analogs, confirming the critical role of lone-pair electrons in mediating interactions with Lys628 of GSPT1.

name: LYG-202
description: This 4-fluorophenylalanine-derived degrader showed limited efficacy (27.12% degradation), likely due to suboptimal spatial orientation of the primary amine group. Molecular docking suggests insufficient interaction with CRBN's His353 residue, underscoring the requirement for specific hydrogen-bond acceptors in this molecular scaffold.

name: LYG-205
description: LYG-205 incorporates a 2-hydroxyacetamide modification, yielding minimal GSPT1 degradation (27.16% at 200 nM). The hydrophilic hydroxyacetamide group may disrupt hydrophobic interactions within the CRBN binding pocket, highlighting steric and polarity constraints for molecular glue design.

name: LYG-206
description: This methyl-protected oxime variant achieved 92.41% GSPT1 degradation at 200 nM with KG-1 IC₅₀ = 4.65 ± 2.08 nM. Methylation stabilizes the labile oxime while maintaining hydrogen-bonding with GSPT1 Lys628. Its oral bioavailability (F = 27.6%) represents a significant improvement over earlier analogs.

name: LYG-207
description: With shortened carbon chain length, LYG-207 showed reduced degradation (38.41%). Altered spatial positioning of substituents compromises the hydrogen-bond interaction with His353 of CRBN, demonstrating the criticality of linker geometry for molecular glue functionality.

name: LYG-301
description: This benzofuran-3-carboxamide degrader induced 82.24% GSPT1 degradation. The fused heterocycle enhances metabolic stability relative to aliphatic analogs while maintaining π-π stacking with Phe150 of CRBN. KG-1 antiproliferative activity (IC₅₀ = 18.85 ± 7.37 nM) confirms cellular efficacy.

name: LYG-302
description: Featuring a benzo[b]selenophene core, LYG-302 exhibited 40.38% degradation. The selenium heteroatom and dimethoxy groups increase molecular weight and polarity, potentially reducing membrane permeability and contributing to its suboptimal degradation profile.

name: LYG-303
description: As a tetrahydroquinoline derivative, LYG-303 achieved 86.36% degradation and KG-1 IC₅₀ = 15.05 ± 3.64 nM. The partially saturated ring system provides conformational rigidity that enhances binding to the CRBN-GSPT1 interface, though microsomal stability remains moderate.

name: LYG-304
description: This 4-oxoquinoline-3-carboxamide showed minimal degradation (23.10%). The planar aromatic system may induce off-target interactions or impede proper orientation in the tri-tryptophan pocket of CRBN, limiting its molecular glue efficacy.

name: LYG-305
description: LYG-305 incorporates a chromone scaffold with 54.99% degradation. The 4-oxo group creates an extended conjugated system that potentially disrupts optimal binding geometry despite theoretical hydrogen-bonding capability.

name: LYG-306
description: With reversed chromone substitution, LYG-306 exhibited 22.33% degradation. The altered position of the carbonyl group relative to LYG-305 demonstrates how subtle structural changes significantly impact molecular glue function.

name: LYG-307
description: This tetrahydronaphthalene degrader showed exceptional 96.02% degradation and potency (KG-1 IC₅₀ = 1.16 ± 0.18 nM). Cyclization enhances metabolic stability (T₁/₂ = 40.51 min) while maintaining key interactions with GSPT1 Lys628. Oral bioavailability remains limited (F = 10.3%).

name: LYG-308
description: The chroman analog LYG-308 achieved 96.06% degradation. Its benzodihydropyran oxygen forms a critical hydrogen bond with GSPT1 Lys628, while the phenyl ring engages in π-π stacking with CRBN Phe150. Microsomal half-life (53.25 min) represents significant improvement.

name: LYG-309
description: Featuring a 6-trifluoromethoxy group, LYG-309 degraded 90.87% of GSPT1. The strong electron-withdrawing substituent enhances degradation efficacy over unsubstituted chromans. KG-1 IC₅₀ = 6.32 ± 2.10 nM confirms cellular activity, though oral exposure remains suboptimal.

name: LYG-401
description: This unsubstituted 2H-chromene degrader demonstrated 72.14% degradation. Introduction of the double bond blocks metabolic oxidation sites, conferring exceptional microsomal stability (T₁/₂ = 369.94 min) and acceptable oral bioavailability (F = 19.28%). Represents a key scaffold optimization.

name: LYG-402
description: With 5-fluoro substitution, LYG-402 showed 76.13% degradation. The fluorine atom's moderate electron-withdrawing effect and small steric footprint enhance target engagement relative to LYG-401, though positional isomers demonstrate variable efficacy.

name: LYG-403
description: The 6-fluoro isomer LYG-403 exhibited reduced degradation (53.81%). Altered electronic distribution from fluorine positioning compromises interactions with key residues in the CRBN binding interface, highlighting position-dependent effects.

name: LYG-404
description: This 7-fluoro analog showed minimal efficacy (52.75% degradation). Steric interference from ortho-positioned fluorine likely disrupts the planar orientation required for optimal molecular glue function.

name: LYG-405
description: LYG-405 (8-fluoro substitution) achieved near-complete degradation (97.48%) with KG-1 IC₅₀ = 2.54 ± 0.96 nM. The para-positioned fluorine optimally enhances electron deficiency without steric conflict, yielding superior target engagement.

name: LYG-406
description: With 6-chloro substitution, LYG-406 induced 85.49% degradation. Chlorine's increased polarizability relative to fluorine provides stronger halogen bonding interactions within the hydrophobic binding pocket.

name: LYG-407
description: This 6-bromo analog showed 79.86% degradation. The larger bromine atom enhances hydrophobic interactions but may induce slight steric strain, explaining its marginally reduced efficacy compared to chloro-substituted analogs.

name: LYG-408
description: Featuring 8-trifluoromethyl group, LYG-408 achieved exceptional degradation (99.34%) and potency (KG-1 IC₅₀ = 3.03 ± 0.35 nM). The strong electron-withdrawing CF₃ group maximizes binding affinity, though its oral half-life (6.95 hr) requires optimization.

name: LYG-409
description: The preclinical candidate LYG-409 (6-trifluoromethoxy) degraded 92.39% of GSPT1 with DC₅₀ = 7.87 nM. It demonstrates oral bioavailability (F = 22.9%), metabolic stability (T₁/₂ = 250.75 min), and in vivo efficacy (94.34% TGI at 30 mg/kg in MV4-11 model). Selective degradation via CRBN recruitment makes it a promising therapeutic candidate.

name: LYG-410
description: With 8-trifluoromethoxy substitution, LYG-410 achieved 99.40% degradation and exceptional potency (KG-1 IC₅₀ = 1.94 ± 0.34 nM). The para-positioned OCF₃ group optimizes electron withdrawal properties for maximal ternary complex formation.

name: LYG-411
description: This 5-methyl analog induced 89.63% degradation. Methyl substitution enhances hydrophobic interactions without significant steric penalty, maintaining favorable binding kinetics within the CRBN-GSPT1 interface.

name: LYG-412
description: The 6-methyl isomer LYG-412 showed 89.15% degradation. Positional effects of methyl substitution demonstrate similar efficacy to LYG-411, indicating tolerance for small alkyl groups at multiple positions.

name: LYG-413
description: Featuring 8-methyl group, LYG-413 achieved 93.37% degradation and KG-1 IC₅₀ = 3.64 ± 0.72 nM. The para-methyl substituent balances hydrophobic enhancement with minimal steric interference, contributing to its potent molecular glue activity.

name: LYG-414
description: With 5-methoxy substitution, LYG-414 induced 93.01% degradation. The methoxy group's dual hydrophobic and hydrogen-bond accepting properties enhance target engagement, though its impact varies by position.

name: LYG-415
description: This 6-methoxy analog showed reduced efficacy (76.84%). The ortho-positioned methoxy group likely causes steric conflict or suboptimal orientation, demonstrating position-sensitive effects of polar substituents.

name: LYG-416
description: The 8-methoxy isomer LYG-416 achieved 89.03% degradation and KG-1 IC₅₀ = 2.14 ± 0.73 nM. Para-positioning of the methoxy group enables optimal hydrogen-bond formation without steric hindrance.

name: LYG-417
description: Featuring 6-chloro-7-methyl disubstitution, LYG-417 showed moderate degradation (72.81%). The adjacent substituents create steric congestion that compromises binding geometry despite individual favorable properties.

name: LYG-418
description: With 6,8-difluoro substitution, LYG-418 achieved 75.12% degradation. Synergistic electron withdrawal enhances affinity but may induce conformational strain, limiting efficacy relative to mono-substituted analogs.

name: LYG-419
description: This 6,7-difluoro analog showed minimal degradation (48.08%). Ortho-difluoro substitution creates severe steric constraints that disrupt optimal binding orientation.

name: LYG-420
description: Featuring 6-tert-butyl group, LYG-420 achieved 90.27% degradation and exceptional potency (KG-1 IC₅₀ = 0.60 ± 0.20 nM). The bulky tert-butyl group enhances hydrophobic burial but increases metabolic liability (T₁/₂ = 19.74 min).

name: LYG-421
description: This 6-phenyl derivative induced 84.90% degradation. The extended aromatic system provides additional π-stacking interactions but may reduce solubility and membrane permeability, limiting cellular efficacy.

name: MDEG-541
description: MDEG-541 is a heterobifunctional PROTAC integrating a 10058-F4-derived MYC inhibitor and thalidomide-based CRBN ligand. It promotes ubiquitin/proteasome-dependent degradation of MYC, GSPT1/2, and PLK1 via CRBN recruitment (rescued by CRBN-KO). Demonstrates antitumor activity in gastrointestinal cancers (mean GI₅₀ = 6.5 μM in organoids), with pleiotropic effects validated by proteomics (>7,000 proteins analyzed).

Compound 619 is a thalidomide-derived molecular glue featuring the linker segment of MDEG-541 but lacking the 10058-F4 MYC-inhibitory moiety. It selectively induces CRBN-dependent degradation of GSPT2 (log₂FC < -1 at 10 μM, 24 h) without affecting GSPT1 or MYC. This reduced neosubstrate scope correlates with diminished antiproliferative activity (MOLM-13 IC₅₀ > MDEG-541), highlighting the critical role of structural components in ternary complex formation.

name: LC-03-052
description: LC-03-052 is an initial hit molecular glue degrader (MGD) targeting NEK7, exhibiting moderate degradation potency with a DC50 of 26 nM and Dmax of 75% in MOLT-4 cells. Its structure includes a tetrahydroimidazo[1,2-a]pyrazine scaffold, facilitating CRBN-dependent ubiquitin-proteasome system-mediated degradation via the G57 degron motif in NEK7.

name: LC-03-041
description: LC-03-041 is a molecular glue degrader lacking the biphenyl tail modification, resulting in significantly reduced NEK7 degradation activity (DC50 >1 μM, Dmax 50%). This underscores the critical role of the biphenyl group in enhancing ternary complex formation and degradation efficacy through CRBN binding.

name: LC-04-039
description: LC-04-039 features a para-chloro substituent on the biphenyl moiety, but shows weak degradation potency against NEK7 (DC50 >1 μM, Dmax 53%). This modification compromises activity, indicating that halogenation at this position disrupts optimal interactions with the degron motif.

name: LC-04-040
description: LC-04-040 incorporates a para-methyl group on the biphenyl tail, restoring partial degradation activity (DC50 0.123 μM, Dmax 76%) compared to analogs. This demonstrates that methyl substitution can improve NEK7 binding affinity in CRBN-mediated ubiquitin-proteasome degradation.

name: LC-04-041
description: LC-04-041, with a para-fluoro substituent, exhibits poor degradation efficiency (DC50 >1 μM, Dmax 56%), highlighting the sensitivity of the para position to fluorine, which may sterically hinder interactions with NEK7's degron residues.

name: LC-04-042
description: LC-04-042 replaces the biphenyl with a 4-pyridinyl group, leading to minimal degradation (DC50 >1 μM, Dmax 28%). This indicates that heterocyclic substitutions are not tolerated for effective CRBN-NEK7 ternary complex formation.

name: LC-04-043
description: LC-04-043 contains a meta-chloro group on the biphenyl moiety, but shows negligible degradation (DC50 >1 μM, Dmax 43%). This meta-position modification fails to enhance potency, suggesting suboptimal steric or electronic effects.

name: LC-04-044
description: LC-04-044 features a meta-methyl substituent, providing moderate degradation activity (DC50 0.192 μM, Dmax 68%). This improvement over chloro analogs reflects better hydrophobic interactions in the NEK7 degron motif for CRBN-mediated degradation.

name: LC-04-045
description: LC-04-045 is a highly potent and selective NEK7 MGD, with a DC50 of 7 nM and Dmax of 90%. Its ortho-chloro substituent enables strong halogen bonding with NEK7 residues, enhancing CRBN-dependent ubiquitin-proteasome degradation and selectivity.

name: LC-04-046
description: LC-04-046 incorporates an ortho-methyl group, yielding reduced degradation (DC50 0.699 μM, Dmax 57%) compared to chloro analogs. This underscores the importance of halogen bonding for optimal degron engagement and potency.

name: LC-04-100
description: LC-04-100, with an ortho-fluoro substituent, shows modest degradation (DC50 0.255 μM, Dmax 62%). Fluorine's smaller size and weaker interactions limit efficacy, emphasizing structural specificity in MGD design for NEK7.

name: LC-04-101
description: LC-04-101 features an ortho-trifluoromethyl group, resulting in very low activity (DC50 >1 μM, Dmax 5%). The bulky substituent likely disrupts ternary complex formation, indicating steric incompatibility in the degron pocket.

name: LC-04-102
description: LC-04-102 includes an ortho-methoxy moiety, demonstrating reasonable degradation (DC50 0.11 μM, Dmax 78%). This substituent supports improved binding, possibly through polar interactions in CRBN-mediated NEK7 degradation.

name: LC-04-103
description: LC-04-103 has an ortho-trifluoromethoxy group, showing weak degradation (DC50 >1 μM, Dmax 27%). The large, electron-withdrawing group impedes efficient NEK7 engagement, reducing ubiquitin-proteasome efficacy.

name: LC-04-104
description: LC-04-104, with an ortho-difluoromethyl substituent, exhibits minimal degradation (DC50 >1 μM, Dmax 20%). This modification is poorly tolerated, highlighting the degron's sensitivity to steric bulk in MGD binding.

name: LC-04-109
description: LC-04-109 incorporates an ortho-cyano group, yielding low degradation activity (DC50 >1 μM, Dmax 28%). The polar cyano moiety likely disrupts hydrophobic interactions critical for NEK7-CRBN complex stability.

name: LC-04-159
description: LC-04-159 combines ortho-chloro and methyl modifications, achieving strong degradation (DC50 0.091 μM, Dmax 86%). This synergistic effect enhances potency through optimized halogen bonding and hydrophobic packing in the NEK7 degron.

name: Compound 1
description: Compound 1 is an uncharacterized molecular glue degrader that induces CRBN-dependent degradation of the zinc-finger protein FIZ1. Identified via DegMS proteomics, it shows dose-dependent FIZ1 degradation blocked by proteasome or neddylation inhibitors, with cellular activity confirmed by NanoBiT and immunoblot assays.

name: 15b
description: This molecular glue degrader exhibits CRBN binding (HTRF IC50 = 1.3 μM) and selectively degrades CK1α (EC50 = 0.22 μM, Ymin = 44%) and SALL4 (EC50 = 0.16 μM, Ymin = 67%). Stereochemistry at distal positions significantly alters neosubstrate specificity, emphasizing its role in targeted protein degradation.

name: 16b
description: With CRBN binding IC50 >10 μM, it moderately degrades GSPT1 (EC50 = 3.1 μM, Ymin = 85%). The cyclopropane modification demonstrates how regiochemistry influences ternary complex formation, reducing degradation depth compared to analogs.

name: 19a
description: A potent molecular glue showing strong CRBN binding (IC50 = 0.16 μM) and deep degradation of IKZF3 (EC50 = 0.012 μM, Ymin = 9.2%), CK1α, and GSPT1. Stereoselective cyclopropenation enhances efficacy, underscoring its utility in neosubstrate-selective degradation.

name: 19b
description: This compound binds CRBN (IC50 = 0.35 μM) but degrades IKZF3 shallowly (EC50 = 0.11 μM, Ymin = 69%). Distal stereochemistry reduces degradation depth, highlighting stereochemical control as critical for optimizing molecular glue function.

name: 20a
description: As a cyclopropene analog, it degrades IKZF3 (EC50 = 0.90 μM, Ymin = 40%), CK1α, and SALL4. Weaker potency than 19a illustrates regiochemical effects on proteasomal targeting, with cyclopropenes generally outperforming cyclopropanes.

name: 20b
description: Exhibiting IKZF3 degradation (EC50 = 3.7 μM, Ymin = 10%) and CRBN binding (IC50 = 35 μM), it confirms cyclopropene superiority over cyclopropanes. Regiochemical positioning near the carbonyl impairs activity, affecting degradation selectivity.

name: 21b
description: It binds CRBN (IC50 = 0.8 μM) and degrades CK1α (EC50 = 0.25 μM, Ymin = 57%) and SALL4 (EC50 = 0.075 μM, Ymin = 68%). Stereochemical variations modulate neosubstrate recruitment, pivotal for designing selective degraders.

name: 22a
description: This cyclopropene derivative degrades GSPT1 (EC50 = 1.4 μM, Ymin = 2.3%) and SALL4, with high selectivity for GSPT1. Its structure exemplifies how sp3-rich elements minimize off-target effects in CRBN-mediated degradation.

name: 22b
description: Efficiently degrades GSPT1 (EC50 = 1.4 μM, Ymin = 1.4%) with CRBN binding (IC50 = 7.8 μM). Stereochemistry fine-tunes degradation depth, reinforcing enantioselective methods for enhancing molecular glue potency.

name: GBD-3
description: A PROTAC-based degrader with a meta-substituted pomalidomide linker (6-atom equivalent), designed to concurrently degrade BTK and GSPT1. It shows moderate BTK degradation (>70% at 50 nM) but limited GSPT1 efficiency due to suboptimal linker length, as per immunoblot analysis in DLBCL cells.

name: GBD-4
description: Features a 6-carbon linker in the PROTAC scaffold, optimized for CRBN recruitment. It induces BTK degradation but exhibits inconsistent GSPT1 downregulation, highlighting linker length constraints for molecular glue-like activity in lymphoma models.

name: GBD-5
description: Equipped with a 7-carbon linker, this dual-mechanism degrader efficiently degrades both BTK and GSPT1 (>70% at 50 nM) by merging PROTAC (BTK ubiquitination) and molecular glue (GSPT1-CRBN stabilization) strategies, enhancing anti-proliferative effects.

name: GBD-6
description: Incorporates an 8-carbon linker for ternary complex formation; it degrades BTK effectively but shows variable GSPT1 degradation, indicating suboptimal molecular glue engagement in concurrent targeting assays.

name: GBD-7
description: With an 8-carbon meta-substituted linker, it robustly degrades BTK and GSPT1 (>70% at 50 nM) via dual mechanisms. Molecular docking confirms its role in stabilizing GSPT1-CRBN interactions, supporting potent cell cycle arrest.

name: GBD-8
description: Designed with a 9-carbon linker, it concurrently degrades BTK and GSPT1 but at lower efficiency than GBD-9. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest compromised molecular glue properties due to linker flexibility in CRBN binding.

name: GBD-9
description: A dual-mechanism degrader with a 9-carbon linker that degrades BTK (80%) via PROTAC and GSPT1 (90%) via molecular glue in 4 hours at 100 nM. It independently recruits CRBN for ubiquitination, showing superior anti-proliferative and apoptotic effects in DLBCL/AML cells.

name: GBD-11
description: Features a 10-carbon linker for extended conformation; it degrades BTK but with reduced GSPT1 efficiency. Proteomics data indicate off-target risks, underscoring the critical role of linker atom count for molecular glue specificity.

name: GBD-13
description: Optimized with an 11-carbon chain, it demonstrates BTK degradation via PROTAC but inconsistent GSPT1 downregulation. Cell viability assays reveal moderate inhibition, highlighting limitations in dual-mechanism design for longer linkers.

name: GBD-15
description: Incorporates a 12-carbon linker, designed to test degradation limits. It shows weak concurrent BTK/GSPT1 degradation, with proteomics confirming inferior selectivity compared to GBD-9, emphasizing molecular glue sensitivity to linker length.

name: GBD-16
description: Utilizes a flexible PEG-based linker to enhance ternary complex stability. It degrades GSPT1 via molecular glue mechanisms, but BTK efficiency is variable, as validated in immunoblot and pull-down assays for CRBN engagement.

name: BTX306
description: BTX306 is a cereblon-binding protein homeostatic modulator featuring a unique thiophene-fused scaffold with a substituted phenylurea and glutarimide. It potently degrades GSPT1, eRF1, CK1α, MCL-1, and c-MYC, inducing caspase activation and apoptosis in multiple myeloma cells. This agent overcomes lenalidomide and bortezomib resistance and demonstrates nanomolar potency in preclinical models.

name: Compound 3f
description: Compound 3f is a pomalidomide-derivatized Class I HDAC selective inhibitor, showing IC50 values of 457.1±5.2 nM for HDAC1 and 433.7±30.1 nM for HDAC2. It induces histone H3 and H4 acetylation, promoting cell cycle arrest at S-phase and apoptosis in hematological tumor cells. Its activity is preserved in lenalidomide-resistant models.

name: Compound 2f
description: Compound 2f is a Class I HDAC inhibitor derived from pomalidomide, with IC50 values of 551.5±3.4 nM for HDAC1 and 378.6±7.1 nM for HDAC2. It selectively increases histone acetylation, leading to caspase-dependent apoptosis and S-phase cell cycle arrest. The compound exhibits nanomolar antiproliferative activity against myeloma cells.

name: F3C-Le (NE-015)
description: F3C-Le is a 6-(trifluoromethyl)-modified lenalidomide derivative that abolishes neosubstrate degradation capabilities. It shows no interaction with IKZF1, SALL4, or PLZF in biochemical assays  and fails to induce degradation of therapeutic targets (e.g., IKZF1, IKZF3) or teratogenicity-associated substrates (e.g., SALL4) in cellular models (Fig. 4d–f). Its bulky substituent disrupts CRBN binding, as confirmed by isothermal titration calorimetry

name: F3CO-Le (NE-016)
description: F3CO-Le features a 6-(trifluoromethoxy) modification on lenalidomide. It exhibits negligible binding to CRBN neosubstrates (IKZF1/SALL4/PLZF) in AlphaScreen assays  and lacks protein degradation activity across all tested neosubstrates . Structural analysis attributes this loss of function to steric hindrance from the bulky substituent, which impedes ternary complex formation.

name: Br-Le
description: Br-Le (6-bromo lenalidomide) demonstrates weak neosubstrate degradation. It minimally degrades IKZF1/IKZF3/CK1α  and shows reduced anti-proliferative effects in multiple myeloma (MM) and 5q myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) cell lines compared to lenalidomide . Its moderate size at the 6-position partially impairs selectivity.

name: Cl-Le (NE-013)
description: Cl-Le (6-chloro lenalidomide) selectively degrades anti-cancer neosubstrates (IKZF1/IKZF3/CK1α) while sparing teratogenic targets (SALL4/PLZF) . It exhibits lower degradation efficacy than F-Le but maintains significant anti-proliferative activity in MM and MDS models . Its selectivity arises from optimized steric interactions with CRBN’s hydrophobic pocket.

name: NE-003
description: NE-003 is a 6-fluoro-pomalidomide derivative that non-selectively degrades both therapeutic (IKZF1) and teratogenic (SALL4) neosubstrates . Unlike 6-fluoro-lenalidomide, it fails to enhance selectivity due to pomalidomide’s intrinsic binding properties, highlighting scaffold-dependent effects on neosubstrate specificity.

name: F-Le (NE-005)
description: F-Le (6-fluoro lenalidomide) potently degrades hematological cancer targets (IKZF1/IKZF3/CK1α) while minimizing degradation of teratogenicity-linked neosubstrates (SALL4/PLZF) . It demonstrates superior anti-proliferative effects in MM and 5q MDS cell lines versus lenalidomide , attributed to enhanced ubiquitination of therapeutic targets.

name: NE-010
description: NE-010 (4-hydroxythalidomide) is listed in the derivative panel , but specific functional data are not provided in the manuscript. Its role in neosubstrate selectivity remains uncharacterized.

name: T4
description: T4 is a quinazolin-4(3H)-one-based molecular glue degrader that induces Cyclin K degradation via the cereblon-DDB1-CUL4 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex. This regulates alternative polyadenylation and suppresses RNA polymerase II phosphorylation, with effects enhanced in phenotypic screening. T4 serves as a chemical tool for probing Cyclin K-dependent pathways.

name: TR-893
description: TR-893 is a structurally analogous compound to TR-213 but functions as a negative control due to its inactivity in alternative polyadenylation reporter assays. It fails to degrade Cyclin K or inhibit RNA polymerase II phosphorylation. TR-893 is used to validate specific molecular glue mechanisms in proteomic studies.

name: TR-213
description: TR-213 is an optimized Cyclin K degrader developed from T4 through structure-activity relationship studies. It exhibits superior potency in degrading Cyclin K and CDK12, robustly regulating alternative polyadenylation activity. TR-213 demonstrates enhanced efficacy in cellular assays compared to its precursor.
